Treifos · Signs of Pure and Impure Animals · Washing and Salting · Basar b'Chalav

By Rabbi Nachman of Tchehrin ז״ל

✦ ✦ ✦

segments.he: כרמלית הוא מקום שאין לו מחיצות ןוגם אינו הילוך לרבים וע"כ מן התורה אינו לא רה"י ולא רה"ר כי אינו מאיר בו הארת החכמה כ"כ וגם אין בו אחיזת הסט"א כ"כ. וכן תל או חריץ שיש בו ד' על ד' ואינו גבוה עשרה נמצא שמרומז בו מבחי' המלכות לבד בלא הארת החכמה בה בשלימו' וע"כ אסרו חכמים להוציא ולהכניס לתוכו בין מרה"י בין מרה"ר מקום פטור הוא מקום שאין בו ד' על ד' שמרמז לבחי' מלכות וגבוה משלשה למעלה אפילו עד לרקיע ממילא אין שם אחיזת החיצונים מאחר שאינו הילוך לרבים וגם א"א להם לקבל חיות משם מאחר שאינו מרומז שם מבחי' המלכות דקדושה ג"כ ע"כ הוא מקום פטור כי אע"פ שבוודאי יש גם שם חיות דקדושה בבחי' מלא כל הארץ כבודו אעפ"כ הוא שם בהעלם מאחר שאין מקום ד' על ד' שמרמז לבחי' מלכות כנ"ל וע"כ אין שייך שם ברורים ע"י מלאכת ההוצאה מרה"י לתוכו או ממנו לרה"ר והוא רק מקום פטור. ואם שגיתי ח"ו והוא רחום יחכפר.
segments.en: [§4] And therefore it is forbidden to walk with an upright, imperious bearing — as if crowding the feet of the Shechinah [Divine Presence] — for in this world, the feet of holiness are clothed, as it were, as is explained in the discourse of Vayeshev-Zicharon, Siman 54 — and this is the aspect of the divine intellect and life-force that exists in every thing — and every one of Israel must bind himself and subjugate his entire bearing, his desires, his character traits, and all his affairs — only beneath the holy intellect — in the aspect of *"and every standing being shall bow before You"* [cf. Yeshayahu 45:23]. Therefore it is also forbidden to walk with an uncovered head — to show that one accepts upon himself the awe of Heavenly Kingship — which is the aspect of the נ [nun], through which the mind in the head merits to receive the higher light of the intellect, which is the aspect of the ח [ches]. And from the words of our Sages it is understood that through this [covering the head] one subdues and weakens the power of the yetzer hara, which is from the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra [other side].

segments.he: וממלא מובן כי א"א לבאר בדברים כאלו כל הצורך מחמת דקות הענינים: וע"כ גם אויר רה"ר למעלה מעשרה הוי מקום פטור. כי שם כבר גובר כח הקדושה (ע"ד שארז"ל מעולם לא ירדה שכינה למטה מעשרה וכו') וע"כ אין שייך שם ברורים.
segments.en:
סִימָן ל׳ וְכוּ׳

[§1]
Now — to explain all types of treifos in detail according to this approach would require great length — and also because the hidden matters are not our domain — to explain the secret of every single aspect and organ of a living creature — and what they allude to spiritually at their root — one must therefore be brief in this. And regarding the law of the cut windpipe — through its majority — and the perforated esophagus — in the smallest amount — this has been somewhat explained above. And were it not for my concern — I would say in a playful manner regarding the matter explained in the Shulchan Aruch, Siman 33: that the outer layer of the esophagus is red and the inner layer is white — etc. — for it is already explained that the windpipe alludes to the aspect of Yaakov — who chose the World to Come — in which there is no eating and drinking — which is the aspect of the windpipe. And this is the aspect of: "the voice is the voice of Yaakov" — the aspect of the windpipe which produces voice — and it is also in the aspect of: "acquire wisdom" [Mishlei 4:5] — which is the attribute of Yaakov. And Esav's hold is in the aspect of the esophagus — where the essential eating and drinking passes — etc. — as all of this is understood in the holy Zohar.

[§2]
And behold: Yaakov and Esav were both in one womb — and even at their birth it is said: "and his hand grasped the heel of Esav" — for the windpipe and the esophagus are by nature joined together in Creation. And therefore: if the esophagus separated from the windpipe — etc. — it is a treifah. For this is Yaakov's quality — not to separate the esophagus — which is the aspect of this world in which there is eating and drinking — from the World to Come — the aspect of the windpipe. For Yaakov too had to use the things of this world — only he did everything with wisdom — and all his deeds were for the sake of Heaven. Not so Esav — who corrupts the order of Creation and separates the aspect of this world from the World to Come entirely — which is the aspect of the esophagus being separated from the windpipe — and therefore it is a treifah — the aspect of the sitra d'mosa.

[§3]
And this is the aspect of: the esophagus — which alludes to the aspect of this world — has two skins. The outer one is red — for in it the aspect of Esav the red one seizes most. And the inner one is white — for the inner dimension of this world is in the aspect of whiteness and brightness — the aspect of the World to Come — the aspect of the thirty-two paths [of wisdom] — whose acronym is lavan [white] — as is known. And therefore: if they were reversed — so that the outer is white and the inner is red — this is from the aspect of Esav — whose inner dimension is from the fierce power of judgment and the lusts of this world — and even when he performs something of holiness — which is the aspect of whiteness — the aspect of chasadim — the aspect of the World to Come — it is only in the aspect of externality — while his inner dimension is the aspect of Esav who is red. Therefore it is a treifah. And likewise if both are red. And if both are white — see in the Shulchan Aruch.

[§4]
And according to the opinion that forbids even this — it is a treifah — for this is the aspect of: *"do not be overly righteous"* [Koheles 7:16] — the aspect of Esav's questions: "how does one tithe straw?" — etc. One may also say: the esophagus — which is the aspect of this world — has in it the hold of Esav and Yishmael. Esav is red — and Yishmael is in the aspect of white — for they also count by the moon — and his suckling is from the side of kindness — the aspect of whiteness — from the side of Avraham. And therefore he is in the aspect of white milk — as stated. And therefore: when Yaakov went to Lavan — to subdue his klippa and clarify from him the holy sparks — as stated in Orach Chaim — then Esav went to Yishmael — etc. — in order to receive even more power from him — and to unite with him against Yaakov. And therefore: if they were reversed — this indicates the cunning of the yetzer hara — the aspect of Esav — dressing itself in mitzvos — which are the aspect of whiteness — but its inner intention is to do harm. And likewise if both are red or white — this indicates that the klippos of Esav and Yishmael united together to overpower Yaakov — and therefore it is a treifah. And likewise: if it has two esophagi or two windpipes — it is a treifah — for: "everything extra is as if removed." And it goes without saying regarding two esophagi — for in it is the essential hold of wicked Esav: "do not be overly wicked" — but even two windpipes — it is also a treifah — the aspect of: "do not be overly righteous." And also: "and do not be overly wise" [Koheles 7:16] — for one's deeds must be more than one's wisdom.

[§5]
And therefore: the essential fullness of acquiring wisdom and the World to Come is through acquiring holy Torah — which is the aspect of the central pillar — as stated. All of this we have written in a somewhat playful manner — as stated. And in truth it is difficult to explain all matters of treifos in detail — for they are numerous. But in general: there are organs that are the vessels of life-force.

[§6]
Such as the brain, the heart, and the lung — and within them too there are details: the skull and the membranes of the brain and the brain itself — and likewise the pericardium and the cardiac muscle and the cardiac chambers and the cardiac tube — and likewise the membranes of the lung and the lung tissue and the bronchial tubes. And there are the vessels of eating — the digestion of food — its purification and clarification — which are the intestines and the proventriculus and the crop and the stomach — etc. — and the liver and the gall bladder and the spleen — etc. — and likewise all of them.

[§7]
And likewise there are vessels of the general structure of the body — such as the spine and the ribs. And vessels of the body's functioning — for standing and walking and lying and resting. And within each of these categories there are many particulars — as stated. And all of them allude spiritually to what they allude to — and everything is encompassed within the aspect of drawing these rectifications — which is the general of all. For Chochmah and intellect is the aspect of the totality of the first three [Keter, Chochmah, Binah]. Torah is the aspect of the central pillar — the aspect of the Vav of the extremities. And Malchus is the aspect of the sof davar [end of the matter] — as is known. And therefore our Sages received the halachic measure of all types of treifos of each and every organ as a law given to Moshe at Sinai — according to its aspect. For there are blemishes that relate essentially to the aspect of drawing Chochmah and intellect — the aspect of life-force. And there are blemishes that flow from having damaged against holy Torah — and the essential is through the sin of neglecting Torah — G-d forbid. And there are blemishes that flow from having damaged the aspect of Malchus. And in all of them our Sages received the true measure — in what manner the blemish can still be rectified easily — and then the treifah that descended through it does not entirely destroy the life-force of the creature — G-d forbid — but it can be healed — and over time it returns to health. And there are those where the blemishes prevailed so greatly — to the point that they affect the life-force — and it does not survive twelve months — as our Sages taught: "a treifah does not survive." And then it is forbidden — for the sitra achra has seized it — and will trap one's soul through this eating — G-d forbid.

[§8]
And therefore: if there is a doubt whether a treifah survived twelve months — or until it became pregnant and gave birth — it is in the presumption of being valid. For from this it is apparent and seen that the sitra d'mosa does not have hold upon it — for: "one who has no support does not produce fruit." And since it became pregnant and gave birth — it is apparent that it is from the side of holiness — which is the aspect of eternal life — the aspect of the world's sustenance through species. And it is in the aspect of what our Sages taught regarding a person — that one who leaves a son behind — etc. — is as if he did not die. And therefore it is said: "pure fat closes the hole" — for it is as the flesh itself — and therefore it naturally adheres to it well and closes. But impure fat — since it is from the aspect of the white of the sitra achra — as stated — it does not adhere as well to the flesh and does not close. And therefore: whatever in cattle corresponds to this is not closing in the chayah either — for it suffices to free itself by what the Torah permitted from the species of chayah — as stated — but not to close and save the creature from treifah — since it too does not naturally adhere to the flesh. But even so the Torah permitted it — as stated.

segments.he: אבל אויר רשות היחיד (שמרמז על הקדושה כנ"ל) הוא רשות היחיד עד לרקיע וע"כ גם אם אין בו ד' על ד' אם הוא גבוה ט' טפחים וליש אומרים אפילו עד עשרה ורבים מכתפים עליו הוי רשות הרבים מאחר שהוא תשמיש לרבים. אבל מעשרה ולמעלה גובר כח הקדושה ומחמת שאין בו ד' אין שייך שם ברורים כי עיקר הבירור ע"י מלכות דקדושה שהיא בחי' ד' כנ"ל: וזה בחי' חיוב של המעביר ד' אמות ברה"ר עצמו ג"כ כי ד' אמות ש לאדם קונות לו והם בחי' רשותו כי אמה מרמז לבחי' ה"א עילאה ולבחי' וא"ו שעל ידם נמשך הארת החכמה כי היא גימטריא המילוי של שם ע"ב כידוע. וד' מרמז לבחי' מלכות ע"כ ארז"ל מיום שחרב בית המקדש (ע"י בחי' התגברות היצה"ר מלכות דסט"א) אין לו להקב"ה בעולמו אלא ד' אמות של הלכה כי שם נמשכין כל התיקונים הנ"ל ע"י שעוסק שם בתורה והלכה. וע"כ כשמוציא חוץ מד' אמות חייב כאלו הוציא מרה"י לרה"ר כנ"ל.
segments.en: [§5] And therefore one must check one's bodily needs — etc. — in order to repel and expel the aspect of Esav, who is called "the wild boar" [Tehillim 80:14] — in the aspect of "go forth — say to it" [cf. Yeshayahu 52:11] — so as not to confuse and disturb the holy intellect and mochin.

segments.he: ובזה תבין ממילא כמה הלכות וענינים המבוארים מסימנים הנ"ל ואילך:
segments.en:
סִימָן מ״ו — הִלְכוֹת בִּרְכוֹת הַשַּׁחַר

 
 [§1]
 And this is the aspect of the Morning Blessings — 
 whose essential foundation is to guide a person so that through every affair and matter 
 he is aroused toward His service and gives thanks and blesses Him 
 for every single thing — 
 for example: upon hearing the rooster crow, one recites "Who gives the rooster understanding" — etc. 
 When dressing, one recites "Who clothes the naked." 
 And likewise "Who opens the eyes of the blind," "Who releases the bound" — 
 and all the rest through "Who removes sleep" — etc.
 

 
 [§2]
 For sleep is the aspect of the temporary withdrawal of daas [knowledge] and mochin — 
 and it is also for the person's benefit, 
 in order that he merit the renewal of the mochin — 
 this being the aspect of "a new face" — 
 for *"a person's wisdom illuminates his face"* [Koheles 8:1]. 
 And therefore specifically when he washes his face, he recites "Who removes sleep."

segments.he: סימן שנ"ח וכו'

וע"כ כל היקף שהוא יותר מבית סאתים כחצר המשכן נתנו חכמים עליו דין כרמלית כי חצר הוא בחי' מלכות כידוע בפרט חצר המשכן וכל שהקיפו מחזיק יותר משיעור זה יצא מבחי' זו וע"כ אין לטלטל בתוכו יותר מד' אמות אלא אם כן הוא מוקף לדירה דאז נעשה טפל להבית שיהיה ג"כ בחי' מלכות כידוע מאחר שדירת הבית קדמה להקיפו:
segments.en:
[§3]
 And what follows it [in the blessing]: 
 "accustom us in Your Torah" — etc. — 
 "and cleave us to the good inclination" — etc. — 
 "and bend our inclination to be subjugated to You" — 
 for one prays about the bending of the yetzer hara, 
 who wants to separate the person from the light of the intellect — 
 and to merit the good inclination [yetzer tov], 
 which is the aspect of misken v'chacham [poor and wise], 
 who guides a person to cleave only to the light of holy wisdom and intellect.
 

 
 [§4]
 And this: "and grant us" — etc. — "chen [grace]" — etc. — 
 for through this one merits the chen mentioned above. 
 And this: "and bestow upon us good kindnesses" — 
 for as is explained in the holy Zohar: 
 "Good — the good itself is wholly within it; chesed that spreads outward" — 
 and this is also the aspect of the illumination of the intellect and the contraction. 
 And this: "Who bestows good kindnesses upon His people Israel" — 
 for thus does Hashem conduct Himself with His people Israel, 
 in the aspect of bestowing good kindnesses: 
 illuminating for them at all times the light of the holy intellect 
 through various vestments and contractions, 
 so that they can receive and benefit from His light. 
 And this is adjacent to the blessing of "Who removes sleep" — 
 for this too is the matter of sleep: 
 in order to receive through it a renewed illumination of the mochin — 
 in the aspect of "they are new every morning" — as stated above. 
 And this: "and save us from the brazen-faced" — 
 the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra, as is known.
 

 
 [§5]
 The one hundred blessings that King Dovid instituted to recite each day — 
 also [serves] to set the heart upon every thing and bless Him 
 until reaching the count of one hundred blessings — 
 which also allude to the two aspects mentioned above, 
 in the secret of the upper pool and the lower pool — as is understood in the Maurai Or. 
 And this he derived from the verse: 
 *"What does Hashem your G-d ask of you?"* [Devarim 10:12] — 
 "Do not read mah [what] but me'ah [one hundred]" — 
 for mah alludes to the attribute of Malchus — as is known — 
 and specifically through this one receives the light of Chochmah, 
 which is the aspect of Aleph — as it is written: 
 *"and He will teach me wisdom"* [Iyov 33:33].

segments.he: סימן שס"ג וכו'

וע"כמבוי שמרמז ג"כ לבחי' מלכות שיש לו ג' מחיצות מן התורה הוא רשות היחיד גמור כי הג' מחיצות הם בצורת בי"ת שהוא בחי' מלכות או בצורת חי"ת שהיא בחי' חכמה כנ"ל ואעפ"כ אסור חכמים לטלטל בו רק ע"י לחי שהוא בחי' יסוד בחי' יוסף או ע"י קורה שהוא בחי' יעקב כמבואר במאורי אור וזה כנגד בחי' יעקב ויוסף המבואר בפנים והם הראשונים שכתוב בהם ששמרו את השבת כמו שדרשו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה:
segments.en: [§1] Therefore one must conduct himself with modesty even in the privy — so as not to sever himself even then from the holy intellect, G-d forbid. For although that is a place of filth where it is forbidden to contemplate Torah matters — and for that reason one must be careful that the forces of the other side not gain hold of him even then — yet by conducting himself even then according to the holy Torah and with modesty, the forces of the other side are unable to gain hold of him even there — for through this he remains bound, in a profound inner way, hidden and concealed, even then, to the holy intellect and wisdom — in the aspect of *"and with the modest [tzne'im] is wisdom"* [Mishlei 11:2].

segments.he: סימן שס"ו

וע"כ תיקנו חכמים לערב עירובי חצירות שלא להוציא מרשות אחד לרשות חבירו אף אם הם דרים בשתי בתים בחצר אחד אם לא ע"י עירוב. כי אין אדם דומה לחבירו במדריגה ועיקר בענין הלימוד הנ"ל של קבלת עול מלכות שמים שלימה והסתכלות באמת רק אל אור השכל דקדושה ע"כ כיון שדר השני בבית בפני עצמו ע"כ אין להוציא לרשותו כ"א ע"י עירוב שאז נעשין כאלו דרים ביחד כי סעודת שבת כלולה מכל התיקונים הנ"ל וע"כ כשנשתתפו ע"י עירוב אז נחשבין שני הרשויות כאחד:
segments.en:
סִימָן מ״ז — בִּרְכוֹת הַתּוֹרָה

 

 
 [§1]
 For meriting all of the above comes through engaging in Torah — 
 and this: "please make the words of Your Torah sweet in our mouths" — 
 for as it is already said: 
 *"the righteous walk in them, but sinners stumble through them"* [Hoshea 14:10] — 
 and our Sages taught: 
 "If one merits, it becomes for him a life-giving potion — 
 for he merits through this to receive the light of Chochmah, which is the aspect of life."
 

 
 [§2]
 If one did not merit — meaning when he follows his evil inclination, G-d forbid — 
 then not only does he not subdue it through Torah study, 
 but on the contrary, at times it grows stronger against him through the cunning 
 that enters him — until he finds a justification for his wickedness 
 from the Torah itself, G-d forbid — as is known — 
 and then it becomes for him a death-dealing potion — 
 for the words of Torah, when they enter his mouth, 
 are so degraded and coarsened that they become the aspect of bitterness — 
 like the waters of Marah — 
 *"and they could not drink the waters of Marah — for they were bitter"* [Shemos 15:23] — 
 meaning, the waters themselves were bitter and repugnant. 
 And like the gravely ill person whose every bite turns to wormwood and bitterness in his mouth.
 

 
 [§3]
 And therefore one prays that one merit for the words of Torah to be sweet and pleasant 
 in one's mouth — and this: "Maharev na" [please make sweet] — specifically — 
 for erev has the sense of aravit [evening] and the withdrawal of light — 
 and also the sense of sweetness and pleasantness — 
 in the aspect of *"and the light is sweet"* [Koheles 11:7]. 
 For through Torah study one merits both these aspects — 
 to the degree that even the contraction — the aspect of Malchus, the attribute of night — 
 is also in the aspect of light — 
 for specifically through it one merits the sweetness of the light of the intellect — as stated.
 

 
 [§4]
 And this: "and may we and our children" — etc. — 
 "know Your Name" — 
 that we merit to know His Name with full knowledge and great understanding. 
 And this: "who study Your Torah for its own sake."
 

 
 [§5]
 And this: "Who teaches Torah to His people Israel" — the Melamayd — specifically — 
 for in every matter and affair that Hashem brings about with us at every time, 
 clothed in every thing, is a great and holy understanding 
 that guides us to draw close to Him 
 and cleave to Him — 
 and this is the essential definition of studying the holy Torah — 
 as it is written: 
 *"and you shall show them the path in which to walk"* [Shemos 18:20].
 

 
 [§6]
 And this: "Who chose us from all peoples and gave us His Torah" — 
 for through the holy Torah He separated us from the nations, 
 who are from the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — 
 the side of the yetzer hara — 
 and through the holiness of the Torah we are rescued from them and subdue them.
 

 
 [§7]
 The Priestly Blessing — adjacent to this: 
 "May Hashem bless you and protect you" — 
 corresponding to the aspect of Malchus — which is the aspect of Shamar [guarding] — 
 and there [in Malchus] is the command: 
 *"for there Hashem commanded the blessing — life"* [Tehillim 133:3] — 
 the opposite of the kingdom of the sitra achra — 
 the side of Esav, of whom it is said: 
 "and he did not desire blessing." 
 And Yaakov our father, through having merited the birthright — 
 the aspect of the bond with the intellect mentioned above — 
 therefore also received the blessing. 
 And our Sages taught: "May He bless you with wealth" — 
 which is from the aspect of Malchus — 
 and *"the rich man rules over the poor"* [Mishlei 22:7] — 
 "and protect you from the destroyers" — 
 which are from the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — the four primary damages — 
 and our Sages also taught: "and protect you from the yetzer hara" — for it is the aspect of the yetzer hara — as stated.
 

 
 [§8]
 "May Hashem cause His countenance to shine upon you" — 
 the aspect of the illumination of the holy wisdom and intellect — 
 which is the essence of life and the light of the face — as stated — 
 as it is written: *"in the light of the king's countenance is life"* [Mishlei 16:15]. 
 And this: "and be gracious to you" — the aspect of chen — as stated. 
 "May Hashem lift His countenance toward you" — our Sages taught: 
 "at the time when you stand in prayer" — etc. — 
 meaning that through this all prayers and requests are accepted. 
 And "and grant you peace" — 
 meaning one will no longer be burdened by any battle against the yetzer hara — 
 the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — 
 only peace and tranquility on every side, 
 and the entire sitra achra will be fully subjugated to holiness.
 

 
 [§9]
 These are the things that have no limit — 
 for this deep learning has no limit whatsoever — 
 for one must engage in this always, all the days of one's life, 
 and go from level to level, 
 meriting at every turn the aspect of a renewed acceptance of the Heavenly yoke, 
 new contractions, and the illumination of the intellect anew 
 at an ever higher and greater level — 
 in the aspect of 
 *"the path of life leads upward for the wise"* [Mishlei 15:24] — as is known. 
 And therefore these things — which allude to this matter — have no limit whatsoever.
 

 
 [§10]
 Pe'ah [the corner of the field] alludes to the aspect of Malchus and contraction — as is known. 
 Bikkurim [first fruits] alludes to the aspect of the illumination of the intellect and wisdom — 
 which is the aspect of bechorah [firstness / the birthright] — 
 the aspect of reishis [beginning / primacy] — as is explained within. 
 Re'ayon [the appearance at the Temple] — the aspect of gazing — 
 that one must gaze only at the intellect in every thing — 
 this being the aspect of the mitzvah of appearing [at the Temple] on the pilgrimage festivals 
 to receive the light of the Divine countenance — 
 as is understood in the discourse Mishra, Siman 30.
 

 
 [§11]
 Gemillas chasodim [acts of lovingkindness] and Talmud Torah — 
 for one must give strength to the yetzer tov — 
 the aspect of the holy Malchus — 
 to overpower the yetzer hara — 
 the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — 
 and this one merits through Torah study — as is explained within. 
 And gemillas chasodim is also needed — 
 in order to sweeten the dinim [judgments] and gevuros [stern powers] 
 from which the nourishment of Esav — the kingdom of the sitra achra — the yetzer hara — draws. 
 And this is what our Sages expounded [Avodah Zarah 5b]: 
 "Happy are you who sow over all waters, sending forth the feet of ox and donkey" — 
 when Israel engages in Torah and acts of lovingkindness, their inclination is given into their hands — as stated.
 

 
 [§12]
 "These are things from whose fruits a person eats in this world 
 while the principal remains intact for the World to Come" — etc. — 
 for our Sages already taught that Yaakov took as his portion the World to Come; 
 and the reward of the World to Come — it is known that the essential reward 
 is the light of attainment and wisdom — 
 to perceive Him in perfect knowledge — 
 and this is the essential occupation of Yaakov even in this world — 
 for "today is the time to act" — 
 and "according to how much a person cleaves in this world" — etc. 
 However, for the time being, while a person is still clothed in a body, 
 he also needs the body's necessities — which are from the side of this world — 
 and his intention in them is only for the sake of the purpose of the World to Come. 
 But for the time being he is also in need of them — 
 and therefore [the Sages] taught: 
 "these are things from which a person eats the fruit also in this world" — 
 but the principal remains complete for him for the World to Come — 
 which is the essential thing for the Jewish person.
 

 
 [§13]
 Returning to the matter of the Blessing over Torah: 
 one who merely thinks about Torah words is not required to recite the blessing — 
 for the essential Torah study through which one gives strength to holy Malchus 
 and merits to receive the light of Chochmah — the essential life — 
 all of this is accomplished through Torah study in full voice — specifically — 
 for Malchus is the mouth. 
 And this is what our Sages taught: 
 "for they are life to those who find them" — 
 "to those who bring them forth through the mouth" — specifically. 
 And therefore according to some opinions, one who listens to words of Torah 
 must also recite the blessing — 
 since his fellow at least brings it forth through the mouth.
 

 
 [§14]
 The prayer Ribon Kol HaOlamim — 
 for "from where shall wisdom be found?" [Iyov 28:12] — 
 and likewise holy Malchus is in the aspect of poor and destitute — 
 only receiving from the aspect of Chochmah — 
 the opposite of the kingdom of the sitra achra, 
 which rules arrogantly without a crown — 
 and is therefore called melech zakein u'ksil [an old and foolish king] — 
 for all arrogance is foolishness. 
 And our Sages taught: if one is wise, his wisdom departs from him. 
 And therefore, immediately in the morning one should arise early and say 
 "Ribon kol ha'olamim" — etc. — 
 to nullify and humble oneself before the holy Malchus and holy Chochmah 
 in complete self-nullification.
 

 
 [§15]
 And this: "What are we, what is our life?" — etc. — 
 "and the advantage of man over beast is nothing — for all is vanity" — 
 for even the wisdom and intellect of a person, 
 if it is not fully bound to holiness, G-d forbid — 
 that too is vanity. 
 And this: "but for the pure soul" — etc. — 
 which is a portion of G-d Above — 
 as it is written: *"and He breathed into his nostrils a living soul"* — 
 and one who breathes, breathes from within himself — 
 and she is the source of holy intellect — as stated — 
 and she will in the future render account — etc. — 
 for every movement that was not completely and perfectly bound 
 to the holy intellect as it should have been.
 

 
 [§16]
 And this: "and all the nations whose souls and wisdom and all their vitality 
 are only from the side of impurity" — 
 therefore they are as nothing before You — etc. — 
 [(and worse than animals and creeping things — as is understood from the words of our Sages)] — 
 and through this we subdue and nullify the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra 
 with a full mouth and complete nullification, 
 so that they not be able to gain hold within us, G-d forbid — 
 and not implant in our minds any of their opinions or reasonings — 
 for all of them are only from the side of the yetzer hara and all is vanity. 
 And this: "but we are Your people, the children of Your covenant" — etc. — 
 "who chose us from all peoples" — 
 and this too not because of our righteousness or the uprightness of our hearts — 
 only because of the love of our forefathers Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov.
 

 
 [§17]
 And this: "the congregation of Yaakov, Your child, Your firstborn" — specifically — 
 the aspect of the birthright that Yaakov merited — as is explained within. 
 And this: because of Your love — etc. — 
 "You called his name Yisrael" — 
 after the aspect of the holy Malchus — from the expression of 
 *"for you have striven"* [Bereishis 32:29] — etc. 
 And Yeshurun is from the expression of gazing and of uprightness — as is known — 
 for he walks only in uprightness and wholeness, 
 through gazing only at the intellect in every thing — 
 through which the intellect illuminates for him in all his ways — 
 in the aspect of *"the path of the righteous is as a shining light"* [Mishlei 4:18] — as is explained within. 
 And there is also another explanation: 
 for Yisrael contains the letters לי ראש — "to me is a head" — 
 after the mochin and the intellect — 
 and Yeshurun is named after the acceptance of the Heavenly yoke of Kingship — 
 in the aspect of *"and He was a King in Yeshurun"* [Devarim 33:5] — see the kavanos.
 

 
 [§18]
 And therefore we are obligated to give thanks to You — etc. — 
 for the pleasantness of our portion — etc. — 
 that we merited to unify His Name twice in love — 
 through the recitation of Shema and Baruch Shem — 
 which also allude to the two aspects mentioned above. 
 For in Shema — etc. — we testify to His unity: 
 that there is nothing besides Him, 
 and in every thing is clothed the holy intellect and His divine life-force — 
 for He gives life and being to all of them. 
 And Baruch Shem [Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever] 
 corresponds to the aspect of נ [nun] — the aspect of Malchus. 
 And through this one can also explain Atah Hu — etc. — 
 that one recites afterwards — as is self-evident.
 

 
 
 
 Returning to the matter of the Blessing over Torah Study —
 ונחזור לענין ברכת התורה
 

 

 
 [§19]
 One who merely thinks about Torah is not required to recite the blessing — 
 for the essential Torah study through which one gives strength to holy Malchus — etc. — 
 and through which one merits to receive the light of Chochmah — the essence of life — 
 all of this one merits through Torah study in full voice — specifically — 
 for Malchus is the mouth [peh]. 
 And this is what our Sages taught: 
 *"for they are life to those who find them"* [Mishlei 4:22] — 
 "to those who bring them forth through the mouth" — specifically. 
 And therefore according to some opinions, 
 one who listens to words of Torah must also recite the blessing — 
 for his fellow at least brings it forth through the mouth.
 

 
 [§20]
 The other Morning Blessings have already been partially explained above. 
 And this too is the matter of Ribon Kol HaOlamim [Master of all worlds] that one recites afterwards — 
 for *"from where shall wisdom be found?"* [Iyov 28:12] — 
 and likewise the holy Malchus is in the aspect of poor and destitute — 
 only receiving from the aspect of Chochmah — as stated — 
 the opposite of the kingdom of the sitra achra, 
 which rules without a crown — only with arrogance and brazenness — 
 and is therefore called melech zakein u'ksil [an old and foolish king] — 
 for all arrogance is foolishness — 
 and our Sages taught: if one is wise, his wisdom departs from him. 
 And therefore, immediately in the morning, one should arise early and say 
 "Ribon kol ha'olamim" — etc. — 
 to nullify and humble oneself before the holy Malchus and holy Chochmah 
 in complete self-nullification.
 

 
 [§21]
 And this: "What are we, what is our life?" — etc. — 
 "and the advantage of man over beast is nothing — for all is vanity" — 
 for even the wisdom and intellect of a person, 
 if it is not fully bound to holiness, G-d forbid — 
 that too is vanity. 
 And this: "save for the pure soul" — etc. — 
 which is a portion of G-d Above — as it is written: 
 *"and He breathed into his nostrils a living soul"* [Bereishis 2:7] — 
 and one who breathes, breathes from within himself — 
 and she is the source of the holy intellect — as stated above — 
 and she will in the future render account — etc. — 
 for every movement that was not completely bound to the holy intellect as it should have been.
 

 
 [§22]
 And this: "and all the nations — whose souls and wisdom and all their vitality 
 are only from the side of impurity" — 
 therefore they are as nothing before You — etc. — 
 [(and even worse than animals and creeping things — as is understood from the words of our Sages)] — 
 and through this we subdue and nullify the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra 
 completely, with a full mouth — 
 so that they cannot gain hold within us, G-d forbid — 
 and not implant in our minds any of their opinions or arguments — 
 for all of them are only from the side of the yetzer hara and all is vanity. 
 And this: "but we are Your people, the children of Your covenant" — etc. — 
 "who chose us from all peoples" — 
 and this too not because of our righteousness or the uprightness of our hearts — 
 only because of the love of our forefathers Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov — 
 as the verse explicitly states regarding this.
 

 
 [§23]
 And this: "the congregation of Yaakov, Your child, Your firstborn" — specifically — 
 the aspect of the bechorah [birthright] that Yaakov merited — as is explained within. 
 And this: because of Your love — etc. — 
 "You called his name Yisrael" — 
 after the aspect of the holy Malchus — from the expression of 
 *"for you have striven"* [Bereishis 32:29] — etc. 
 And Yeshurun is from the expression of gazing and of uprightness — as is known — 
 for he walks only in uprightness and wholeness, 
 gazing only at the intellect in every thing — 
 through which the intellect illuminates for him in all his ways — 
 in the aspect of *"the path of the righteous is as a shining light"* [Mishlei 4:18]. 
 And this is the aspect of *"the path of the righteous is upright"* [Yeshayahu 26:7] — etc. — 
 and it is written: *"Know Him in all your ways"* [Mishlei 3:6] — 
 the aspect of gazing at the intellect mentioned above — 
 and through this: "and He will straighten your paths." 
 And regarding the Torah in general — through which one merits all of the above — 
 it is said: *"for the ways of Hashem are upright"* [Hoshea 14:10] — etc. 
 And there is also another interpretation: 
 that Yisrael is called [לי ראש] — "to me is a head" — 
 after the mochin and the intellect — 
 and Yeshurun is named after the acceptance of the yoke of Heavenly Kingship — 
 in the aspect of *"and He was King in Yeshurun"* [Devarim 33:5] — see the kavanos.
 

 
 [§24]
 And therefore we are obligated to give thanks to You — etc. — 
 for the pleasantness of our portion — etc. — 
 that we merited to unify His Name twice in love — 
 in the recitation of Shema and Baruch Shem — 
 which also allude to the two aspects mentioned above. 
 For in Shema — *"Hear O Israel — Hashem is our G-d — Hashem is One"* — 
 we testify to His unity: 
 that there is nothing besides Him, 
 and in every thing is clothed the holy intellect and His divine life-force — 
 for He gives life and existence to all of them. 
 And Baruch Shem [Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever] 
 corresponds to the aspect of נ [nun] — the aspect of Malchus. 
 And through this one can also explain Atah Hu — etc. — 
 that one recites afterwards — as is self-evident from what was said.
 

 

 
 
 
 סִימָן מ״ח–מ״ט — פ' הַתָּמִיד, הַקְּטֹרֶת, וְסֵדֶר הַתְּפִלָּה

 

 
 [§1]
 And this is the aspect of the passage of the Tamid [daily offering], 
 the passage of the Ketores [incense], 
 and Eizehu Mekoman [the Mishnaic chapter on sacrifices] — etc. 
 For through all of these one subdues the hard klippos in the world of Asiyah — 
 which are from the side of Esav, the kingdom of the sitra achra — 
 the aspect of the yetzer hara — 
 and one elevates the good and the vitality within them 
 in the secret of the eleven spices of the Ketores — 
 clothing the aspect of Malchus of Asiyah — 
 and Malchus clothes the Netzach, Hod, Yesod — etc. — 
 up to Infinite — as it were — 
 as is alluded to in the discourse Emtzausah, Siman 24 — 
 and see the discourse Ashray Zarka, Siman 35 and Siman 280.
 

 
 [§2]
 All of this is understandable in part through our approach as well — 
 for this is the essential thing: 
 to subdue the aspect of the yetzer hara and the kingdom of the sitra achra so completely 
 that the good and the vitality of the holy sparks clothed within them 
 will rise up to animate them — 
 and they will become a throne and chariot toward holiness — 
 in the aspect of *"with all your heart — with both your inclinations"* [Berachos 54a] — 
 until through this specifically one merits great attainments 
 and to ascend at every turn from level to level, 
 until one merits to attain the aspect of the light of the Infinite, may He be blessed — as stated.
 

 
 [§3]
 And since all of this one merits through the holy Torah — 
 therefore one included in this very section Scripture, Mishnah, and Gemara — 
 as explained in Shulchan Aruch Siman 50. 
 And when one merits to subdue the yetzer hara and the klippos 
 at this level and give strength to the holy Malchus — 
 one then ascends to a level and a greater attainment. 
 But even there at that level, 
 there is a yetzer hara that seeks to overpower the person — 
 in the aspect of "whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than him" — 
 and all of this for the preservation of the power of free will in the human being — as is known. 
 And therefore one immediately recites Kaddish — 
 which has great power to subdue the klippos.
 

 
 [§4]
 Afterwards one recites Hodu — etc. — 
 and many verses proclaiming the greatness of the Creator 
 and the utter nullification of the sitra achra — 
 in the aspect of *"for all the gods of the nations are vanities"* [Tehillim 96:5] — 
 and likewise Mizmor Shir Chanukas — etc. — 
 and the verse "Hashem reigns" — etc. — 
 and through all of this one gives yet greater strength to holiness 
 to overpower the sitra achra and nullify it completely.
 

 
 [§5]
 Afterwards one begins Pesukei d'Zimrah [verses of praise] — 
 corresponding to the aspect of the world of Yetzirah, 
 which corresponds to the Vav in the holy Name — 
 which is the aspect of Torah — as is known. 
 And one connects through this the aspect of Asiyah — 
 the aspect of the Heh in the Name — 
 the aspect of Malchus. 
 And through this one merits to receive the light of the holy wisdom and intellect — 
 which is the root of the light of all lights — 
 and this is the aspect of Birkas HaMaoros [the blessing on the luminaries] that follows.
 

 
 [§6]
 One also includes the blessings of Shema and Shema itself alongside them — 
 for Shema is the aspect of the totality of Torah — as is known — 
 and contains the Ten Commandments — as our Sages taught — 
 for the totality of all these rectifications 
 one merits only through Torah study, 
 which encompasses everything. 
 And it contains the mention of the Exodus from Egypt — 
 which is the aspect of the subjugation of the kingdom of the sitra achra.
 

 
 [§7]
 And afterwards one prays Shemoneh Esrei [the Amidah] — 
 which is the totality of prayer — 
 for through this all prayers and requests are accepted, 
 as one merits chen. 
 And therefore one begins Pesukei d'Zimrah with the verse 
 *"May the glory of Hashem endure forever"* [Tehillim 104:31] — 
 and as is cited in the kavanos: 
 "K'vod Hashem" [the glory of Hashem] in numerical value equals chen — 
 as stated above. 
 For in truth the holy Name whose numerical value is chen 
 encompasses all four holy Names — 
 Av, Sag, Mah, Ben — 
 which are the root of all four worlds — 
 corresponding to which all four parts of the holy prayer were instituted — as is known.
 

 
 [§8]
 Now, to explain the entire order of prayer in detail according to this theme 
 would overflow the available space — 
 and in particular since we do not engage in hidden matters. 
 Nonetheless, some brief allusions to main headings may be offered:
 

 
 [§9]
 Baruch She'amar v'hayah ha'olam [Blessed is He Who spoke and the world came into being] — 
 through this we bless the aspect of the holy vitality and wisdom 
 clothed within all of Creation — through which one can recognize Him 
 through every thing. 
 Baruch Hu [Blessed is He] — through this we bless the totality of His greatness 
 and the essence of the light of His G-dliness before Creation and after Creation — etc. 
 And this: the initials of Baruch She'amar v'hayah ha'olam spell Bashuva [in return / equality] — 
 for before Him, as it were, all is equal — 
 for *"I Hashem have not changed"* [Malachi 3:6] — 
 "You are He before the world was created, and You are He after the world was created" — etc.
 

 
 [§10]
 Baruch Omair v'Oseh [Blessed is He Who speaks and acts] — 
 on the general governance of the world even now after Creation — all only in His providence 
 and with great compassion. 
 Baruch Chai la'ad [Blessed is the Ever-Living] — 
 for only He is the vitality of all the living — etc. — 
 and even the power and vitality of the kingdom of the sitra achra — 
 the sitra d'mosa — is also from Him — as it were. 
 Baruch Podeh u'Matzil [Blessed is He Who redeems and rescues] — 
 for He redeems and rescues from them — 
 as our Sages expounded on 
 *"rescuing the poor from one stronger than him"* [Tehillim 35:10] — 
 referring to the rescue from the yetzer hara. 
 Baruch Shemo [Blessed is His Name] — 
 shem [name] is the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of the holy Malchus — 
 as is cited in the discourse Anochi, Siman 4.
 

 
 [§11]
 And since all prayers, songs, and praises are from the aspect of Malchus — as is known — 
 which is the aspect of how Dovid HaMelech founded upon this the entire Book of Tehillim — 
 therefore one extends this [section of Baruch She'amar] 
 until concluding: "the King Who is praised with praises." 
 And since the essential perfection is to bind the nun to the ches 
 and to include all in a single unity — 
 and Echad [one] in numerical value equals 13 — 
 therefore this praise contains 13 times Baruch [blessed].
 

 
 [§12]
 And it contains 87 words — the numerical value of Levanah [moon]. 
 And through Baruch Chai la'ad — inclusively — 
 there are 9 times Baruch — 
 corresponding to the Heh and the ches in Echad. 
 And this concludes Chai la'ad — for ches is the aspect of vitality — as explained within. 
 And from Baruch Podeh u'Matzil — which alludes to the subjugation of the kingdom of the sitra achra 
 and the affirmation and strengthening of the holy Malchus — 
 there are 4 times Baruch — corresponding to the Dalet in Echad — 
 which alludes to Malchus — as stated. 
 And since Malchus must be bound to the ches — the vitality of all the worlds — 
 therefore it concludes: "the One and Only — the Living One of the worlds — King" — etc.
 

 
 [§13]
 And therefore one recites Mizmor l'Todah [a psalm of thanksgiving] afterwards — 
 which is the aspect of the World to Come — 
 for our Sages taught: 
 "all prayers will be nullified in the future — but thanksgiving will not be nullified. 
 And all sacrifices will be nullified except the thanksgiving-offering" — 
 for then the yetzer hara and all the klippos 
 and all the aspects of the kingdoms of the sitra achra will be nullified — 
 and then all sins will be nullified, and all troubles and sufferings — 
 and *"Hashem shall be King over all the earth"* [Zechariah 14:9] — 
 and *"the earth shall be full of knowledge of Hashem"* [Yeshayahu 11:9] — 
 for then all Israel will merit the aspects of ches and nun 
 with great completeness and wonderful illumination. 
 And therefore there will be then only the aspect of todah [thanksgiving / acknowledgment].
 

 
 [§14]
 And therefore even in this world, when one draws these rectifications, 
 one recites Mizmor l'Todah — 
 and in particular on Shabbos one recites 
 "Mizmor — Tov l'hodos laHashem" [it is good to give thanks to Hashem — Tehillim 92]. 
 And this entire psalm — as well as Yihi K'vod Hashem 
 — in which the 18 verses correspond to the aspect of the ches — 
 and the subsequent verses of praise — 
 and the Song of the Sea — which also contains 18 verses — 
 and Yishtabach — which contains 13 praises — 
 all of this proceeds and is arranged in this same way — 
 and it is all clear of itself following our approach — 
 as well as the blessings of Shema and Shema and the mention of the Exodus — 
 and the eight times the word emes [true] in Emes v'Yatziv — 
 for emes is the totality of the holy mochin — 
 and the mochin and Chochmah are the aspect of ches — as stated.
 

 
 [§15]
 The Amidah — Shemoneh Esrei — and in this [prayer] there is also need to explain some details — 
 but it would take too long. 
 But at any rate it is self-evident: 
 there are 12 intermediate blessings corresponding to the aspects of the ches and the Dalet — 
 besides the blessing against heretics [Bircas HaMinim] — 
 in which one explicitly prays for the nullification of the wicked kingdom and its root 
 in a very high place — as is understood in the kavanos. 
 And one begins with Atah Chonen la'adam daas [You grace man with knowledge] 
 and "and grace us from You" — etc. — 
 and one prays there for the light of the intellect and knowledge and chen — 
 as our Sages taught: "and He will be gracious to you with knowledge." 
 And then one prays for repentance and forgiveness and pardon and redemption — etc. — 
 all of which are included in the rectification of the holy Malchus 
 and the drawing-down of the light of daas. 
 And through this one merits that all prayers are accepted — 
 and this is why one concludes with Shome'a Tefillah [Who hears prayer] — 
 and there too the aspect of holy chen is alluded to — 
 as one prays: "be gracious to us and answer us" — etc.
 

 
 [§16]
 And this is what one says at the end of the prayer: 
 "Act for the sake of Your Name" — the aspect of Malchus — 
 "Act for the sake of Your right hand" — 
 which subdues the kingdom of the sitra achra — as it is written: 
 *"Your right hand, Hashem, shatters the enemy"* [Shemos 15:6] — 
 "Act for the sake of Your Torah" — 
 through which one gives strength to holy Malchus — as stated — 
 "Act for the sake of Your sanctity" — 
 the aspect of Chochmah, which is called Kodesh. 
 And therefore all who say this each day merit and receive the face of the Shechinah — 
 as cited in the Tur — for this is the aspect of gazing at the divine vitality.
 

 
 [§17]
 Afterwards one falls on one's face to raise the holy sparks clothed in the 
 sitra d'mosa — the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — 
 which is the opposite of holy Chochmah — the essence of life — as stated. 
 Afterwards one recites Tehillah l'Dovid — Yihu l'ratzon — 
 through to Aleinu — 
 corresponding to the abundance flowing from Atzilus to Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah. 
 And Tehillah l'Dovid [Psalm 145] corresponds to the aspect of Malchus — 
 the aspect of Dovid's kingship — the alphabet-acrostic of Tehillah l'Dovid 
 corresponding to the 22 letters of Malchus — the mouth — 
 and the letter nun does not appear in it — 
 because there is in it a downfall of the Community of Israel — 
 the aspect of Malchus, which is itself the aspect of nun — 
 and yet Dovid returned and supported her with the holy spirit — as our Sages taught. 
 And Mizmor Yaankha — "May Hashem answer you — may the Name of the G-d of Yaakov protect you" — 
 corresponding to the aspect of the light of the intellect — 
 the aspect of Yaakov — who illuminates even in dark and difficult places — 
 and "He shall send your help from the holy place" — 
 which is the aspect of Chochmah — as is known. 
 And U'va l'Tzion Goel [A redeemer shall come to Zion] — 
 corresponding to the aspect of Torah — 
 for the future redemption comes only in the merit of the holy Torah — 
 as is explained in the holy Zohar — and as stated — 
 for through Torah one gives strength to holy Malchus. 
 And therefore verses were instituted therein so that Israel should read in Torah every day — as our Sages taught.
 

 
 [§18]
 And therefore one recites Aleinu — through which one subdues the klippos — 
 and one prays abundantly for the revelation of His Kingship — 
 "and all shall accept the yoke of Your Kingship" — etc. — 
 and one concludes: "On that day Hashem will be One and His Name will be One."

 Simanim 8–25 (Tzitzis): Tzitzis embodies Malchus/nun — the garment-vessel that makes the infinite light receivable. The four corners = four worlds; the 32 threads = 32 paths of wisdom; the five knots = five Books of Torah; the four threads doubled to eight = the union of Dalet (Malchus) and ches (Chochmah). The small Tallis (worn always, even at night) maintains the ibur-level bond with the intellect; the large Tallis is for prayer — the yenikah-level; Tefillin represents the fully expanded mochin d'gadlus. A borrowed Tallis is exempt because spiritual rectification is personal — no one can stand in for another's free will.
 Simanim 25–45 (Tefillin): The hand-Tefillin (nun) precedes the head-Tefillin (ches) — first the vessel, then the light. The four portions of the hand-Tefillin are in one compartment (the lesser feminine consciousness); the four portions of the head-Tefillin are in four separate compartments — four levels of the great mochin. One must not interrupt between them — the union of ches and nun must be seamless. Black = tzimtzum. The square = Dalet/Malchus. Torah study itself fulfils the essence of Tefillin ("that the Torah of Hashem should be in your mouth"), but Tefillin are still required during Shema and the Tefillah.
 Siman 46 (Birchos HaShachar): Every morning blessing links a physical awakening-event (the rooster, dressing, washing) to the inner spiritual process. Each act is a tzimtzum-level vehicle by which the light of the renewed mochin enters the world. The 100 blessings of Dovid HaMelech = 100 portals of reception, corresponding to the union of mah (Malchus) and aleph (Chochmah).
 Siman 47 (Birchos HaTorah): Torah study is both the vehicle and the destination. Through it one gives strength to Malchus, subdues the yetzer hara, and receives the light of Chochmah. But this requires inner purity — for Torah studied without inner alignment can be twisted by the yetzer hara into a rationalization for evil. The blessing "Maharev na" — with its double meaning of "evening" and "sweetness" — captures this paradox: even the darkness of tzimtzum becomes sweet when Torah illuminates it. The Priestly Blessing is expounded phrase by phrase through the lens of ches-nun-chen. The section then returns explicitly to the Torah blessing (Venachzor l'inyan Birchas HaTorah): one who merely thinks Torah is not required to bless — for Malchus is the mouth; only spoken Torah fulfils the essential bond. The prayer Ribon Kol HaOlamim teaches complete self-nullification before G-d: the nations, whose vitality is from impurity, are as nothing; Israel, chosen by ancestral merit, is called Yisrael (לי ראש — "to me is a head" / the intellect) and Yeshurun (gazing uprightly at the intellect in every thing). The section closes with the double affirmation of Shema (Chochmah — testifying to G-d's oneness pervading all things) and Baruch Shem (Malchus — accepting His Kingship) — the two aspects united.
 Simanim 48–49 (Tamid, Ketores, and the Order of Prayer): The daily sacrificial passages serve to subdue the tough klippos of Asiyah and elevate their inner sparks — transforming the yetzer hara itself into a chariot for holiness. This is the prerequisite for prayer. The entire structure of Pesukei d'Zimrah moves from Asiyah (Malchus) through Yetzirah (Torah-Vav) toward the reception of supernal Chochmah. Baruch She'amar's 13 instances of Baruch = Echad (13). The 18 verses of Ashrei, the 18 verses of the Song of the Sea, and the 18 blessings of the Amidah all mirror the ches-motif of vitality. The Amidah's intermediate blessings begin with Daas (knowledge/grace) and proceed through the full spectrum of rectification, culminating in Shome'a Tefillah — "Who hears prayer."
