[§5] And as the Shulchan Aruch states: corresponding to this, there are ten words in the blessing HaMotzi — ten words in the verse *"He causes grass to grow for the cattle"* [Tehillim 104:14] — meaning: in this verse it is alluded that in order to merit the aspect of Chochmah — which is the essential life and definition of the human being — it is impossible [to achieve this] except through the aspect of Malchus — alluded to in the word behemah [cattle] — as is known. And therefore the verse begins: "He causes grass to grow for the cattle" — and then: "to bring forth bread from the earth." And therefore it is forbidden to eat before feeding one's cattle first — as stated above. And there are also ten words in the verse *"the eyes of all look to You with hope"* [Tehillim 145:15] — for one must know that all livelihood flows only through trust [in G-d] — and one merits trust only through wisdom and intellect — as explained in Siman 225. And there are ten words in the verse *"a land of wheat and barley"* [Devarim 8:8] — for the Land of Israel is the aspect of Malchus — as is known — and receives its abundance from the supernal Chochmah — in the aspect of: the air of the Land of Israel makes one wise. And therefore it contains ten levels of sanctity — corresponding to Chochmah — the aspect of Yud — the aspect of Kodesh. And there are also ten words in the verse *"and He will give you"* — [Bereishis 27:28] — for all influences and all blessings flow in their root from the aspect of Chochmah — which is the source of blessing.

סִימָן רמ״ב — לְהִזָּהֵר בִּכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת

 
 [§1]
 The matter of Shabbos has already been partially explained in the book 
 Yikara d'Shabbata [that appears in the source work]. 
 But nonetheless I said to explain here also some main headings of this.
 

 
 [§2]
 For the holiness of Shabbos encompasses the completeness of all the holy rectifications mentioned above — 
 for Shabbos is the aspect of tachlis [ultimate purpose] of heaven and earth — 
 and the ultimate purpose of all is only 
 "in order that they know Him" — as stated — 
 and this is impossible except through the rectifications mentioned above. 
 And therefore they are all encompassed in the holiness of Shabbos.

[§3]
 For Shabbos is the aspect of Shabbas Malkesa [the Sabbath Queen] — 
 the aspect of holy Malchus — 
 and corresponding to her is the first Shabbos meal on Friday night — 
 the aspect of Chakkal Tapuchin Kadishin [the holy orchard of apple trees] — as is known. 
 And on Shabbos shines the light of supernal Chochmah — 
 the aspect of Kodesh — 
 and corresponding to this is the aspect of 
 seudasa d'Atika Kadisha [the feast of the Holy Ancient One] — 
 for He is the source of Chochmah — 
 the aspect of ches — the aspect of vitality — 
 and therefore *"those who taste it merit life"* [Shabbos liturgy]. 
 And in it is the completeness of Torah reading — through which one gives strength to holy Malchus. 
 And in it is the completeness of the acceptance of prayers — as is known. 
 And this is the aspect of 
 *"and as for me, my prayer is to You, Hashem, at an auspicious time"* [Tehillim 69:14] — 
 which one recites on Shabbos at Minchah.
 

 
 [§4]
 And this is the aspect of the honor of Shabbos — 
 for all the aspects mentioned above are the aspect of kavod [honor]: 
 Chochmah — the 32 paths of Chochmah correspond in number to kavod — 
 in the aspect of *"the wise shall inherit honor"* [Mishlei 3:35]. 
 Torah — in the aspect of: "there is no honor except Torah." 
 Malchus — the aspect of the Melech HaKavod [King of Glory]. 
 Prayer — the aspect of kavod — as explained in the discourse Emor, Siman 2.
 

 
 [§5]
 And this is the aspect of oneg Shabbos [Shabbos delight] — 
 and it is explained in the holy Zohar that the letters of עֹנֶג [oneg] 
 are an acronym for עֵדֶן נָהָר גַּן [Eiden — Nahar — Gan] — 
 which also allude to the aspects of Chochmah, Torah, and Malchus — 
 which is the aspect of prayer — as is known.

[§6]
 And therefore one is careful to eat fish on Shabbos — 
 for dag [fish] is called in the language of our Sages nun — 
 in the aspect of the nun mentioned above — 
 and this is the aspect of einah pekicha [the open eye] of fish — 
 alluding to Chochmah — 
 in the aspect of *"and the eyes of them both were opened"* [Bereishis 3:7] — 
 which was said concerning wisdom — as stated. 
 And therefore Yosef — who merited most fully to the aspects mentioned above — 
 his children were blessed with the blessing of fish — 
 as it is written: *"and they shall multiply like fish"* [Bereishis 48:16] — and as our Sages taught.
 

 
 [§7]
 And this is the aspect of the holiness of the Shabbos meal — 
 for it has already been explained above 
 that during weekday eating there is a hold for the aspect of Esav — 
 whose hold is in the gullet and the liver — the implements of eating — 
 and therefore one must be especially careful then 
 not to give them nourishment beyond their sustenance. 
 But Shabbos eating is entirely holy — 
 as is explained in the discourse Sha'alu et Rabbi, Siman 57. 
 And therefore the Shulchan Aruch states that it is forbidden to eat the bread of non-Jews on Shabbos. 
 And it is customary to knead sufficient dough at home 
 to fulfil the mitzvah of challah and produce loaves for Shabbos — 
 for Shabbos eating is holy, 
 and it is forbidden for non-Jews to have any hold in it.
 

 
 [§8]
 And one sanctifies the bread — which is the essential meal — 
 with additional holiness through kneading the measure of challah 
 and fulfilling thereby the mitzvah of separating challah — 
 which is called reishis [beginning/firstness] — 
 the aspect of Chochmah — as is explained within. 
 And challah is also the aspect of the Shechinah — 
 as is explained in the holy Zohar and the Tikkunnim — 
 the aspect of holy Malchus that receives from Chochmah — as stated. 
 And this is what is cited in Likutay Torah of the Ari, Parshas Shelach — 
 that the mitzvah of challah corresponds to the aspect of 
 the Chochmah d'Nukva [feminine Wisdom] — etc. — 
 as is cited in the Maurai Or.

[§9]
 For challah is the aspect of the Shechinah when joined with the Forefathers — 
 for this too is the aspect of Shabbos holiness: 
 שִׁין בַּת [shin-bas] — 
 the aspect of the Forefathers — whose root is in the three holy mochin — 
 and bas [daughter] is the aspect of the Shechinah — Malchus. 
 And this is the aspect of chen — and through this all prayers are accepted. 
 And therefore it is explained there that challah is also the aspect of prayer — 
 in the aspect of *"and Moshe implored [vayechal]"* — as stated.
 

 
 [§10]
 [(Author's note: See the book Yikara d'Shabbata which brings from the holy Zohar 
 that on Shabbos Hashem Himself, as it were, receives the prayers of Israel. 
 And therefore our Sages taught: 
 "good is a handful with quiet" — this is Shabbos — 
 the aspect of "words spoken in quietness are heard" — as explained within.)]

סִימָן רמ״ב וְכוּ׳

[§1]
The laws of honoring one's teacher and Torah scholars. A person is obligated in the honor and awe of one's teacher — more than of one's father.

[§2]
Meaning: because father and mother are in the aspect of distant causes for drawing these rectifications — as opposed to one's teacher — who is in the aspect of a close cause for this. For through studying Torah with him — one thereby merits to draw these rectifications in their fullness. And therefore one is obligated in his honor and awe — corresponding to the two aspects mentioned — the aspects of Chochmah and Malchus — as stated. And therefore: one who disputes with his teacher — it is as if he disputed with the Shechinah — etc. For since he brings one to know one's Creator and draw close to Him — therefore when one damages his honor — it is as if — G-d forbid — one damaged the honor of the Shechinah — as it were.

[§3]
And therefore: it is forbidden for a student to rule on a halachah in front of his teacher. For the teacher and student are the aspects of sun and moon — as explained elsewhere. And the moon is in the aspect of having nothing of its own — only what it receives from the light of the sun — the aspect of supernal Chochmah — the aspect of the teacher. And therefore one must not rule on a halachah before him — for this shows as if one has some power and light of one's own — independently of one's teacher — who is against one in the aspect of the sun — the aspect of Chochmah. And therefore one is liable to death for this — through having separated from one's teacher's wisdom — the aspect of: "they shall die without wisdom." And therefore: it is forbidden for a student to call one's teacher by name. For: "what is His Name — this is Chochmah" — as cited in the holy Zohar. And when one calls one by name — one shows as if one has already attained the aspect of one's teacher's wisdom — which is the aspect of one's name. And this is a great damage — for the essential aspect of the student — the aspect of the moon — is to know that one has no attainment at all in one's teacher's wisdom — and to anticipate and hope each time to receive from afar some aspect of illumination and glimmer from the light of his wisdom. And through this specifically can one merit that the moonlight be as the sunlight — the aspect of what our Sages taught: Torah only endures in one who makes oneself as if one does not know — as it is said: *"and wisdom — from where shall it be found?"* [Iyov 28:12] — which is itself included in what is elaborated in the discourse mentioned — that because the light of the intellect is very great — one can only merit it through the aspect of nun — the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of the moon — etc. — as stated. And this is what our Sages taught: one who prevents one's student from serving one — it is as if one withholds from one kindness — whose root is in the aspect of Chochmah — as is known — and removes from one the fear of Heaven — the aspect of Malchus — as stated. And: every student who treats the honor of one's teacher lightly — causes the Shechinah to depart from Israel. For through this one causes the aspect of separation — G-d forbid — until one grows distant from Him. And therefore: one does not give honor to a student in front of his teacher — etc. — and likewise several other laws in Siman 242 — and all are explained according to the above.

[§4]
And therefore: Torah scholars are exempt from taxes and levies — and the like. And if one has merchandise — others sell one's merchandise first. And all of this — because through their Torah they give strength to holy Malchus to prevail against the kingdom of the sitra achra. And therefore our Sages taught: one who accepts upon oneself the yoke of Torah — removes from oneself the yoke of the kingdom and the yoke of worldly concerns. And therefore Torah scholars do not need a guard either — for Malchus itself — the aspect of shamor [guarding] — guards them. And therefore one must stand before every Torah scholar — and honor him — even a young sage. For since he merited wisdom — through which His honor is revealed — by knowing and recognizing Him through the intellect and wisdom in every thing — therefore one must honor him — for he is in the aspect of: "the wise shall inherit honor." And likewise: it is a commandment to stand before one who has reached seventy years of age. For even though there is in truth wondrous intellect in each and every thing and matter that passes upon a person — by the hundreds and thousands every single day — in fine particulars. But in general: every single day there is a wondrous intellect through which one must attain and recognize Him according to the aspect of that day. And this intellect is in the aspect of the encompassing intellect of that day — in which all the particular intellectual aspects clothed in every thing that passes upon one on that day are included. And this: *"blessed be Hashem each day"* [Tehillim 68:20] — and our Sages taught: each and every day — give one something from the quality of its blessings. (And see in the tale of the Seven Beggars.) But even the encompassing intellect of each day is the aspect of the particular intellect relative to the encompassing intellect that a person must attain in each year according to its aspect. And the encompassing intellect of the entire year is the aspect of the particular intellect relative to the intellect and attainment that a person must attain in the general days of one's life — which are seventy years. For the fullness of the attainment of knowledge and wisdom for each person according to one's aspect is through multiplying days and years — the aspect of: "five years old for Scripture — ten for Mishnah" — etc. And this is the aspect of: "teach us to count our days — and thus we shall acquire a heart of wisdom" [Tehillim 90:12] — and: "and great years shall make wisdom known" [Iyov 32:7].

[§5]
And therefore: one who has lived out one's days — to be seventy years of age — even if one is an ordinary person — one must honor and stand before one. For the aspect of old age and length of days flows at its root from supernal Chochmah — which is the source of life and length of days — the aspect of: "in the aged is wisdom — and in length of days — understanding" [Iyov 12:12]. And this is the aspect of what our Sages taught [Kiddushin 33]: Rabbi Yochanan would stand before aged non-Jews — saying: "how many troubles have passed over them." For even through the troubles and events that pass upon non-Jews over many days and years — those possessed of holy intellect can also recognize and attain the wonders of the Creator — it emerges that even through this the honor of Heaven can be magnified. And this is the aspect of: "rise before the aged" [Vayikra 19:32] — the aspect of one who is seventy — the aspect of old age — which is from the aspect of the light of Chochmah — from which is the essential life and length of days — and: "the splendor of the face of an elder" — one who has acquired the wisdom of Torah — even a young sage.

[§6]
And this corresponds to the aspect of Torah study. And: "you shall fear your G-d" — this corresponds to the aspect of holy Malchus — where is the source of awe — the aspect of the awe of Malchus. And this: "I am Hashem." For through all of this His divinity is revealed — and one merits to know and recognize Him — and draw close to Him through every thing in the world — as stated.

[§6] One must place salt on the table — for salt also alludes to the person's intellect and wisdom — for according to nature, everything depends on the abundance of saline content in one's constitution — as the scholars of alchemy clarified. And the commentators explained through this the intent of our Sages' words [Kiddushin 29b]: "if a son is sharp and well-seasoned" — etc. And therefore in the Temple it is said: *"upon all your offerings you shall offer salt"* [Vayikra 2:13] — for sacrifices are primarily intended to break the animal spirit and foolishness within oneself — which is from the side of the yetzer hara — in the aspect of *"the sacrifices of G-d are a broken spirit"* [Tehillim 51:19] — and to merit holy Chochmah — therefore salt is prescribed with them.

סִימָן רמ״ג — הַמַּשְׂכִּיר חֲנוּת וּמֶרְחָץ לְעַכּוּ״ם

 

 
 [§1]
 For the holiness of Shabbos was given only to Israel and not to non-Jews — 
 as it is written: *"between Me and the children of Israel"* [Shemos 31:17] — 
 and as our Sages taught: 
 "A non-Jew who rests on Shabbos is liable to death." 
 And our Sages taught [Bereishis Rabbah, Shemos]: 
 a parable of a king and his matron sitting facing one another — etc.

— 
 for during the weekdays — which are the days of labor — 
 and labor is performed in order to clarify and elevate the holy sparks from within the sitra achra — 
 therefore [the sitra achra] has some hold and connection 
 with the aspect of holy Malchus — 
 in the aspect of: "this is Jerusalem which I have set in the midst of the nations" [Yechezkel 5:5] — 
 for she must descend among them to clarify from them the holy sparks.

But on Shabbos the Shechinah rests, as it were — 
 and "when Shabbos enters she is unified and separated from the other side" [Zohar] — 
 and "all the dominions of anger flee and depart from her and there is no dominion elsewhere in all the worlds" [ibid.].

[§7] The table atones like the altar — for the time of eating is a time of battle — as is explained in the holy Zohar. In its plain sense, one must at that time battle with one's desires — which are only from the side of the yetzer hara — and fulfil what our Sages said: "at a meal that gives you pleasure, withdraw your hand from it." And in its inner dimension, the eating itself is a form of battle — for one draws out at that time very holy sparks that were until then clothed within such physical grossness and waste — and all of this is only through the power of bonding to holy Chochmah — for "all of them are clarified through thought" [Zohar] — and therefore it too atones like the altar — and requires salt. And therefore one must speak words of Torah at the table — for the entire power of holy Malchus to overpower the sitra achra and extract what it has swallowed — all of this is only through the power of Torah study — as stated.

Therefore no labor is permitted on Shabbos — 
 and even upon the thought of labor our Sages cautioned: 
 "cease from the thought of labor."
 

 
 [§2]
 And therefore we separate from non-Jews on Shabbos in the most complete separation — 
 for "then all who work iniquity will be separated" [Tehillim 92:10] — 
 and therefore even instructing a non-Jew to perform a prohibited act on Shabbos — 
 amirah l'akum — is [rabbinically] forbidden.

[§8] Lechem u'Melach [bread and salt] in numerical value equals Yosef — for Yosef merited both aspects most fully — and therefore he merited chen [grace] — as is explained within. And therefore it is said of him explicitly: *"and Yosef — he was the ruler"* [Bereishis 42:6] — the aspect of Malchus — and it is said of him: *"there is none as discerning and wise as you"* [Bereishis 41:39] — the aspect of Chochmah.

[§9] And therefore one is particular to bless over the whole loaf — which alludes to Chochmah — as stated — and also over the larger [loaf] and the more beautiful — which alludes to Malchus and greatness — as it is said: *"a king in his beauty your eyes shall behold"* [Yeshayahu 33:17]. And likewise regarding wisdom: *"a person's wisdom illuminates his face"* [Koheles 8:1]. And the essential ascent of a person from the aspect of smallness to the aspect of greatness [gadlus] is only in the matter of the mochin and Chochmah — the aspect of mochin d'gadlus — the aspect of gadol da'as [great in knowledge]. And likewise the essential perfection of Malchus is when it is complete — in the aspect of what our Sages taught: "one who wishes to accept upon himself the complete yoke of Heavenly Kingship" — and its essential completeness is when it is joined with its Beloved and receives from the light of holy Chochmah — as stated — and then it is called sheleimah [complete] — for it completes all things — as is known.

For since the non-Jew does the labor on the intention and thought of the Jew — 
 it is as if the Jew performed the labor — 
 and this would give yet more power to the sitra d'mosa — 
 and therefore the Torah says mechaleleha mos yumas [one who desecrates it shall die] — 
 and even via a non-Jew through rabbinic decree it is forbidden — 
 and even maras ayin [the appearance of wrongdoing] 
 is a concern in this context — 
 for the osos [signs] of Shabbos — 
 שִׁין בַּת — allude to the aspects of 
 shemen [oil] and pessilah [wick] — 
 the aspects of Chochmah and Malchus — 
 and the eyes [ayin] — the aspect of the beholder — 
 correspond to the three colors of the eye which are the aspect of the three holy mochin.

But if the non-Jew acts entirely on his own account 
 and in a manner that involves no maras ayin — it is permitted.

[§3]
 And likewise what is explained in Siman 246 
 regarding the resting of one's animal — 
 for a Jew's animal also alludes to [that spiritual dimension] — 
 as understood somewhat from what was explained above 
 regarding *"You save man and beast alike, Hashem"* [Tehillim 36:7] — 
 for behemah [animal] alludes to the aspect of Malchus — 
 and therefore one is commanded regarding its resting — 
 as it is written: *"you shall not perform any labor — you — etc. — and your animal"* [Shemos 20:10].

[§1] One does not speak during the meal — even words of Torah — lest the windpipe precede the gullet — for in the matter of the meal, the entire affair explained regarding Yaakov and Esav is found — as the verse says: *"the first one came out red"* [Bereishis 25:25] — etc. — and: *"and afterwards his brother came out, with his hand grasping the heel of Esav"* — etc. — and Yaakov gave Esav bread and a pottage of lentils — *"and he ate and drank and rose and went, and Esav despised the birthright"* — and its Targum [Onkelos]: "and Esav cast off the birthright." And it is cited that Esav's hold is in the aspect of the veshet [gullet] — in the aspect of "and Esav cast off" — the aspect of this world, which involves eating and drinking — all through the gullet. And Yaakov is in the aspect of the kaneh [windpipe] — in the aspect of "acquire wisdom" [Mishlei 4:5] — the aspect of the World to Come, which has no eating or drinking.

סִימָן רמ״ה וְכוּ׳ — הִלְכוֹת מְלַמְּדִים וְתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה

[§1]
The laws of teachers and Torah study. The positive commandment upon each person to teach one's son Torah — etc. For the essential purpose of bearing children is b'gin d'yishtamodain leih — in the aspect of: "a father shall make known to the children Your truth" [Yeshayahu 38:19]. And since the essential acceptance of the yoke of Heavenly Kingship and the drawing of holy intellect — through which one merits to know and recognize Him — is only through Torah study — as stated — therefore one must teach one's son Torah. And if his son is wiser and more understanding than him — his son takes precedence in Torah study — for the essential thing is holy intellect. And therefore: it is a commandment to teach also one's son's son Torah — the aspect of Yaakov — who merited the light of holy intellect — and was the grandson of Avraham our father. And therefore: it is a commandment for every sage of Israel to teach students — for since one has merited the light of Chochmah — to the point of being called a sage — therefore one must illuminate from one's light of wisdom also to others. For this is the essential quality of light — that it shines and comes to others. And therefore: when the son of each Jew begins to speak — one teaches him the verse: "Torah commanded us — Moshe" [Devarim 33:4] — and the verse: "Hear O Israel" — etc. For through this one begins initiating him in Torah study — through which strength is given to holy Malchus — the aspect of: "Hear O Israel" — the aspect of acceptance of Heavenly Kingship. And therefore one assigns one teacher for twenty-five students — corresponding to the twenty-five letters of the verse Shema Yisrael. And therefore the value and greatness of the study of young schoolchildren is very great — since it is from the breath of the mouth in which there is no sin — the aspect of the pure breaths of holy Malchus. For in them there is not yet the hold of the vain breaths of the sitra achra — flowing from the side of the yetzer hara — the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra. And therefore their study is most precious — and the world is sustained through it.

And therefore one does not teach Torah to an unworthy student — for since one's inclination has already overpowered one and one has followed its counsel — one can damage through one's Torah study even more — in the aspect of: "if one did not merit — it becomes a deadly poison" — G-d forbid. And therefore one must first return one to the right path — and draw one toward holiness — and then teach. And therefore: a person is obligated in Torah study all the days of one's life — until the day of one's death. For since the essential holy life-force — the aspect of the light of holy Chochmah — one merits through the aspect of Malchus — and the essential power of holy Malchus is through Torah study — therefore: whether poor or rich — in all that passes upon a person all the days of one's life — one is obligated to set fixed times for Torah. For in all that passes upon a person — one must only gaze at the inner intellect in all of this — and this one merits only through Torah study. And therefore one must be constantly fixed in Torah. And therefore a person must divide one's years in three: one third in Scripture — the aspect of the source and foundation of Torah — corresponding to the aspect of the source of holy intellect. One third in Mishnah — the Oral Torah — corresponding to the aspect of Malchus-of-mouth — and it is called the Oral Torah. And through it one can merit the light of the intellect in Scripture — for without the Oral Torah one cannot at all attain the true intention of the Torah — because of the great brilliance of the light in it. It is the aspect of the moon.

And one third in Talmud — corresponding to the aspect of the light that the moon receives from the light of the sun — until the moonlight becomes as the sunlight — the aspect of Talmud — which explains the reasons of the Mishnah — and thoroughly combines and encompasses Oral Torah with Written Torah — through the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded — and the like. And therefore some say: through the Babylonian Talmud one fulfils one's obligation for everything — for it is the general totality of all.

And therefore: it is forbidden to study external wisdoms — and all the more so those that incline toward heresy — G-d forbid — which are the yetzer hara — the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — G-d forbid. And therefore one may not wander in the orchard of other wisdoms — even casually — until after one has filled one's belly with Shas and the legal authorities — and is thoroughly expert in the entire Torah. For otherwise — when one enters those wisdoms — even permitted ones — the sitra achra that suckles from there can overpower one even more. And therefore: Torah study equals all the commandments — for through it one merits the aspects of these rectifications — which are the general totality of all.

[§2]
And therefore: a person does not learn the greater part of one's wisdom except at night. For because of the greatness of Chochmah — one can only merit it through the aspect of Malchus — which is the aspect of night. And therefore: all who study Torah at night — a thread of kindness is drawn upon them — whose root is in supernal Chochmah — as stated. And the thread of kindness is in the aspect of chen [grace] in the language of our Sages — for through this one merits holy grace — as elaborated in the discourse Ashrei mentioned. And therefore: when one finishes a tractate — it is a commandment to rejoice and make a feast. For the conclusion — the sof davar — is in the aspect of Malchus — the source of joy — and all aspects of meals of mitzvah and holy eating and drinking — as is known. And therefore one says then: hadran alach — etc. — da'atan alach — etc. Hadar corresponds to the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of: "glory and majesty of His kingdom" — and also the aspect of splendor and grace — the aspect of: "beauty and splendor — bestow upon him." Da'as corresponds to the light of daas and Chochmah. And some interpret hadran from the language of: "who desires [hadar] to return" — from the language of return [chazarah] — that one returned to one's learning. For since one has merited to finish the tractate — the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of sof davar — and through this very act one merits the light of Chochmah — the aspect of firstness — therefore one must immediately return to one's learning — to the beginning of the tractate. And even if one does not actually go back and study that tractate from the beginning immediately — even so one must at the end of the tractate — at least have one's mind and thought still firmly bound to the beginning of the tractate. And through this one joins the aspect of the moon with the sun — and merits holy grace — as stated. And this: "we shall not forget you" — etc. — "and you shall not forget us" — etc. — the aspect of connection and bond mentioned. L'ra b'alma hadein — v'lo b'alma d'atei — which is itself also the aspect of these rectifications — the aspects of holy Chochmah and holy Malchus. And likewise: the souls of Israel with holy Torah are also the aspect of the connection and union of these two aspects. And therefore one says this at the end of the tractate — in order to unite and strengthen the aspect of the holy connection and union in its fullness.

[§2] During eating, the food passes through the gullet — the aspect of Esav — and the liver is nourished first — which is also the aspect of the red Esav — and afterwards it sends [nourishment] to the heart and the brain — which are the aspect of Yaakov. And when one eats with proper intention — in the aspect of *"the righteous eats to satisfy his soul"* [Mishlei 13:25] — minimizing bodily desire — then he is in the aspect of "the elder shall serve the younger" — for even though the body is nourished first, everything is only for the sake of the soul and holy life-force — which is Chochmah. And this itself is the aspect of the salt — for during the meal, even though the act of eating and drinking is from the side of Esav, one should nevertheless endeavor to be in the aspect of "and his hand grasps the heel of Esav" — to break one's desire — and in one's thought to direct even one's eating solely for the sake of Heaven — for the sake of life and sustenance in the service of one's Creator.

סִימָן רמ״ז וְכוּ׳ — הִלְכוֹת צְדָקָה

[§1]
The laws of charity. It is already explained above that charity is also the aspect of drawing these rectifications. For through a rich person having mercy on a poor person — the aspect of: "praiseworthy is one who considers the poor" — and bestowing upon him — through this: spiritually too — the light of Chochmah — the aspect of the sun — the aspect of wealth and generosity — is drawn to holy Malchus — the aspect of poverty and lowliness — the aspect of the poor wise man. Therefore: charity is called shemesh — "sun of righteousness" — for it is in the aspect of drawing the sunlight — the light of Chochmah — as stated. And therefore: Torah too — through which one also draws the light of Chochmah — is also called charity: "tzedakah da oraisa" [charity — that is Torah]. And therefore it is forbidden to avert one's eyes from charity — for one must gaze at all times with an open eye upon the light of the intellect in every thing. And therefore all who avert their eyes from it — it is as if one worshipped idolatry — for this is from the aspect of the sitra achra — the sitra d'mosa — G-d forbid. And therefore: charity saves from death — and adds life and length of days — and makes wealthy. For Chochmah is the essential life.

[§2]
And the fullness of Malchus is in the aspect of holy wealth — as stated. And therefore: there are eight [ches] levels of charity — each greater than the one — as explained in Siman 249. And this corresponds to the light of Chochmah — which is the aspect of ches — as elaborated in the discourse within.

[§3]
And therefore it is good to give a coin to the poor before prayer — for through this the prayer is accepted — as understood within. And therefore: charity collectors who have charitable funds in their hands — let them marry off poor orphan girls — etc. — for through this charity the holy union mentioned — achieved through charity — is most evident and visible. And therefore one allocates charity for the dead — and it benefits their souls. For through the rectification drawn through charity to holy Malchus — until it is elevated from the aspect of the hold of the sitra d'mosa — the aspect of: "her feet descend to death" — (and see also the discourse Vayiven, Siman 67) — through this: rectification flows also to the souls of the dead. And especially to those dead ones for whom charity is specifically allocated. But for a completely wicked person it does not help — as explained in the Shulchan Aruch — for the completely wicked are from the aspect of the sitra achra — the aspect of what is forbidden to teach Torah to an unworthy student — as stated.

[§4]
And therefore: one must not give charity to one who intentionally transgressed any one of the commandments stated in the Torah — as explained in Siman 251. And therefore: a woman who comes to marry and unite with her partner — the aspect of the union of nun and ches elaborated within — therefore one must not diminish for her less than fifty zuz — corresponding to the aspect of nun mentioned. And therefore: residents of the Land of Israel take precedence in charity over residents of outside the Land — for they are more encompassed in the aspect of holy Malchus — which is itself the aspect of the Land of Israel — as is known. And therefore it is especially a commandment to support Torah scholars — for through the study of their Torah they draw the aspects of these rectifications. And therefore: even through the charity given to them — these rectifications flow more fully. And therefore: the charity of redeeming captives is very great — more than all charities. For through this — the rectification is most evident to the eyes — in the actual act of performing the mitzvah itself. For one is redeeming a soul of Israel — the aspect of holy Malchus — from the hands of non-Jews — the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra. And this is the essential rectification of charity — as stated. And for a Torah scholar — and even only for a sharp student — one redeems him even for a great sum — for upon him depends the rectification of holy Malchus. And therefore: one does not accept charity from non-Jews — for through this they receive — G-d forbid — even more power. And therefore: a king or minister of non-Jews who sent charity — let it be given to poor non-Jews — etc.

[§5]
And therefore: a community may not impose taxes and levies from charitable funds. For honor comes through charity as is fitting — giving strength to holy Malchus. And through this one is freed from all taxes — which are the aspect of the opposite of this — as it is written: "and they placed over them tax officers" — etc.

[§3] And it is precisely through eating that Esav sold the birthright to Yaakov, and afterwards received the blessing too — for in truth, one who binds himself only to the intellect in every thing and thinks only of the ultimate purpose — the World to Come — has in truth also all the blessings of this world in their fullness — in the aspect of *"for G-d has been gracious to me and I have everything"* [Bereishis 33:11]. And therefore afterwards when Esav said to him: "let us journey and go, and I will go alongside you" [Bereishis 33:12] — implying: be like me — Yaakov replied to him: this is impossible — for the world of this side — the aspect of Esav — and the World to Come — the aspect of Yaakov [which in truth encompasses all the good of this world as well] — are two absolute opposites, like darkness and light — and they cannot coexist together. And therefore: "Let my master please pass before his servant" [Bereishis 33:14] — etc. — for first comes darkness and then light — and yet in truth even the darkness is for the benefit of the light — for the advantage of the light is only evident from within the darkness.

סִימָן רמ״ח — יְצִיאַת שַׁבָּת

 

 
 [§1]
 And therefore one may not set sail at sea, 
 nor join a caravan fewer than three days before Shabbos — 
 for three days before Shabbos the illumination of the coming Shabbos's holiness 
 begins to shine — as is known — 
 and they correspond to the aspects of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah — 
 which are also the aspects of the three rectifications mentioned above — 
 namely: the yoke of Heavenly Kingship, Torah, and Chochmah.

And therefore one must prepare oneself from that time 
 to receive the coming Shabbos's holiness in its fullness — 
 and guard oneself from having any distress or confusion on Shabbos — 
 and certainly not to come to any desecration of Shabbos, G-d forbid. 
 But for a matter of mitzvah it is permitted even within the three days — 
 for this is the ultimate purpose of all the rectifications — 
 to fulfil His commandments — 
 and one trusts in Hashem that He will save him from all distress 
 and from any desecration of Shabbos.

[§4] And therefore during the meal — even though one is obligated to speak words of Torah — at the very moment of actual eating it is forbidden to speak even words of Torah — lest the windpipe precede the gullet — for the mouth of the windpipe may open and some food may enter it and bring danger — for it is impossible for them to function together simultaneously — for "Esav is a man who knows hunting, a man of the field" [Bereishis 25:27] — and "Yaakov is a wholesome man dwelling in tents" — in the tent of Torah. And therefore during actual eating one must be silent — directing one's thought in great holiness for the sake of Heaven. But since, for the sanctity of thought — which is the aspect of Chochmah — one must give strength to holy Malchus to overpower [the sitra achra], especially during eating and the meal — when one is drawing out clarifications — one must engage in words of Torah — but not during actual eating.

[§5] Yaakov Avinu did not die — for since the attribute of Yaakov is to look only at the wisdom and life-force in every thing — and even all physical things, like eating, he performs only with this intention — certainly the sitra d'mosa has no hold upon him whatsoever, and he is alive forever.

סִימָן רמ״ט — שֶׁלֹּא לִקְבֹּעַ סְעוּדָה בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת

 

 
 [§1]
 And therefore it is forbidden to establish a feast and banquet on Erev Shabbos — 
 unless it is an obligatory [mitzvah] meal at its proper time — etc.

— 
 And people of exemplary conduct fast every Erev Shabbos — 
 for it has already been explained that the essential completeness of holy eating is on Shabbos — 
 for then Esav — the sitra achra — has no hold in the eating and the meal.

And therefore one must prepare oneself for this — 
 to be eager to eat on Shabbos — 
 and to defer and prevent oneself from a weekday meal 
 in honor of the Shabbos meal — 
 and thereby to subdue the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — 
 the yetzer hara — the dominion of Esav — 
 [whose hold is in weekday eating] — 
 before the Shabbos meal when holy Malchus ascends in its fullness. 
 For Yaakov is the first of whom it is written that he kept Shabbos — as our Sages taught.

[§6] And since the life-force clothed in every food is only from the holy sparks of Chochmah clothed within it — it is forbidden to treat foods with contempt — for Chochmah is in the aspect of honor — as it is said: *"the wise shall inherit honor"* [Mishlei 3:35] — the opposite of the aspect of Esav — of whom it is said "and Esav despised" — as stated.

סִימָן ר״נ — לְהַשְׁכִּים בְּבֹקֶר יוֹם ו׳

 
 [§1]
 One should rise early in the morning on Friday to prepare for Shabbos' needs — 
 for our Sages taught: 
 "One who labored before Shabbos will eat on Shabbos" — etc. — 
 for Shabbos is the aspect of the World to Come — 
 for then one will merit to receive from the light of supernal holy Chochmah in its fullness — 
 which is the essential life of the World to Come — 
 in the aspect of "the righteous sit and benefit from the radiance of the Shechinah" — 
 that they will merit to attain His G-dliness in full attainment — through the aspect of Malchus.

[§2]
 But not all will be equal then — 
 and "every Tzaddik is burned by the canopy of his fellow" [Bava Basra 75a] — as our Sages taught — 
 for everything is according to the abundance of one's deeds. 
 And the more a person strives in this — 
 even in this world, to accept upon himself the complete yoke of Heavenly Kingship 
 and to bind himself and look only at the wisdom and intellect and divine life-force 
 in every thing — 
 the more he merits this in the World to Come — 
 in the aspect of: 
 "one who labored on the eve of Shabbos will eat on Shabbos."
 

 
 [§3]
 And therefore one must hasten to engage in this from one's very youth — 
 for *"precious is one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world"* [Avos 4:17] — etc. — 
 and there is no loss like the loss of time — 
 for it has already been explained that in every moment and time 
 is clothed a new wisdom of how to recognize Him 
 and draw close to Him through it. 
 And therefore even regarding the practical preparation of Shabbos — 
 one must also rise early on Friday morning.

[§4]
 And therefore one must repent every Erev Shabbos — 
 to rectify through one's repentance whatever one may have damaged 
 in the days of the week — 
 through following one's yetzer — 
 the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — 
 which is the opposite of the holiness of Shabbos.
 

 
 [§5]
 And therefore one should remove cobwebs from the house on Erev Shabbos — 
 for they are from the aspect of the sitra achra — 
 the kingdom of Esav — as our Sages expounded on the verse 
 *"a spider grasps with its hands"* [Mishlei 30:28].

[§6]
 And this: the mitzvah to taste from the Shabbos dishes on Erev Shabbos — 
 for our Sages taught that Yaakov took as his portion the World to Come — 
 and yet he is also of necessity obligated to pass through this world — 
 only that in truth the aspect of Yaakov 
 has no desire or will for any worldly matter — 
 rather even his this-worldly affairs are only for the World to Come — 
 and all his actions are only for Heaven's sake. 
 It follows that in his this-world as well he tastes the flavor of the World to Come — 
 and this is alluded to in the tasting of the Shabbos dishes on Erev Shabbos.
 

 
 [§7]
 And one should strive to personally prepare something for Shabbos' needs — 
 for the mitzvah is better performed directly than through an agent — 
 for through every mitzvah holiness is drawn upon the person — 
 in the aspect of "Who sanctified us with His commandments" — 
 and Kodesh is Chochmah — as is known — 
 and therefore one merits through this 
 to bind oneself to holy Chochmah in its fullness 
 through the aspect of the mitzvah — which is the aspect of holy Malchus. 
 And the greater one's effort for the sake of the mitzvah, the greater the reward — 
 and the greater the holiness one merits — 
 for through the effort and strength invested in performing the mitzvah 
 one gives strength to holy Malchus to overpower the kingdom of the sitra achra. 
 And therefore the mitzvah is certainly better performed directly — 
 especially the mitzvah of preparing for Shabbos — 
 which is itself called Kodesh.
 

 
 [§8]
 And therefore one should sharpen the knife on Erev Shabbos in honor of Shabbos — 
 and this is derived from: 
 *"and they shall prepare [v'heichinu] what they bring"* [Shemos 16:5] — 
 אֵת alludes to the aspect of Malchus — 
 and sikkin [knife] also alludes to the aspects of Malchus and Binah — 
 see the Maurai Or.

סִימָן רנ״ב–רס״ז

 
 [§1]
 It is permitted to begin labor on Erev Shabbos near twilight 
 even though the labor completes itself on Shabbos [Siman 252] — 
 for the essential clarifications that are clarified through labor 
 all occur only through the power of Chochmah — which is called reishis [beginning] — as stated. 
 And therefore when the beginning and commencement of the labor — 
 which is performed by the person who possesses wisdom and intellect — 
 takes place before Shabbos — 
 even if it is then completed on Shabbos on its own — there is no concern — 
 since the person does nothing more — 
 it all happens through the power of the beginning made before Shabbos. 
 Except when there is concern he may assist in the labor on Shabbos itself — 
 such as lest he stoke the coals — in that case it is forbidden. 
 And in this is also explained what is stated in Simanim 253, 254, 255, 257, 258, and so on.

[§2]
 They would sound the shofar on Erev Shabbos to separate the people from labor [Siman 256] — 
 for the blasts of the shofar are the aspect of the arousal of the mochin 
 from their slumber — as is known. 
 For the wisdom and mochin of the weekdays are the aspect of mochin d'katnus [small consciousness] — 
 the aspect of sleep — compared to the mochin one merits to receive on holy Shabbos. 
 And therefore on the weekdays they are days of labor — 
 and therefore one sounds [the shofar] on Erev Shabbos 
 to separate the people from labor 
 and prepare them to receive the holiness of the Chochmah and mochin that shine on Shabbos. 
 And this too is the aspect of the blasts themselves — 
 as our Sages taught: 
 "the sounding of the shofar is wisdom and not labor."
 

 
 [§3]
 The mitzvah of bathing in hot water on Erev Shabbos [Siman 260] — 
 and it is explained in the kavanos that this is the secret of 
 the flame of fire that descends on Erev Shabbos to subdue the klippos — 
 meaning one draws the illumination of supernal Chochmah — 
 the aspect of Yaakov and Yosef — who are the aspect of the flame of fire — as stated — 
 as it is written: 
 *"and the house of Yaakov shall be fire and the house of Yosef a flame"* [Ovadyah 1:18] — 
 and through this one burns and subdues the klippos — 
 the aspect of Esav — the kingdom of the sitra achra — 
 the aspect of the yetzer hara's fire — 
 for from fire they came and fire will consume them. 
 And this is the aspect of: 
 "always let a person arouse the good inclination against the evil inclination" — 
 and the arousal is from the aspect of judgments and gevuros — the aspect of fire. 
 And afterwards one immerses in the mikveh — 
 which is the aspect of encompassing oneself in the waters of supernal chesed — 
 which flow from the aspect of the holy supernal intellect — 
 the aspect of chesed and mercy.

[§4]
 Three things one must say at twilight on Erev Shabbos [Siman 260 cont.]: 
 "Did you tithe?" — corresponding to the aspect of Malchus — 
 the aspect of maaser [tithe] — 
 "Did you make the eruv?" — corresponding to Torah study — 
 as explained in the Tikkunnim: 
 eruv is the middle pillar — the aspect of Torah — as is known — 
 "Light the lamp" — corresponding to the illumination of supernal intellect 
 that shines even in the dark — 
 in the aspect of: *"for You light my lamp, Hashem — my G-d illuminates my darkness"* [Tehillim 18:29].
 

 
 [§5]
 The Shabbos lamps [Siman 261] — 
 and it is explained in the kavanos that they correspond to 
 Binah and Malchus — 
 meaning Malchus then receives the illumination of supernal Chochmah through Binah — 
 for they are the two companions that never separate — as is known. 
 And this is the aspect of: 
 "One who wishes to become wise should face south — for the Menorah is in the south" — as our Sages taught. 
 And this is the aspect of the setting of the table on Shabbos — 
 for Malchus ascends then from the aspect of poverty to the aspect of wealth — 
 in the aspect of the royal table — 
 in the aspect of: "one who wishes to become wealthy should face north — for the Table is in the north."

[§6]
 And therefore it is a mitzvah to honor Shabbos in fine garments — 
 for it has already been explained that 
 the supernal intellects are the aspect of the garments of honor of the person — 
 and therefore it is a mitzvah to wear white garments then — 
 corresponding to the supernal whiteness — 
 in the aspect of *"and streams from Lebanon"* — 
 from the whiteness of the brain [levunah d'mocha]. 
 And לָבָן contains the letters ל-ב-ן — 
 which are the initials of: lamed-beis nativot — 
 the thirty-two paths of Chochmah — 
 and also ל״ב נוּ״ן — lamed-beis and nun — 
 meaning one binds the nun — the aspect of Malchus — 
 to the 32 paths of Chochmah.
 

 
 [§7]
 And therefore one is strict about the Shabbos lamps — 
 that the oil and wicks should be valid — 
 so that the oil flows after the wick — 
 for the wick alludes to Malchus and the oil to Chochmah — as is known — 
 and therefore they must be joined and unified in a complete union — 
 that no aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra of Chochmah and Malchus 
 should have any hold — G-d forbid — 
 so that the holy light burns well and does not go out — 
 and so that one not come to desecrate Shabbos.

[§7] Intermediate waters [between courses] are optional — for this alludes to one who has already merited to bind himself to the holy intellect in every thing — and who has actual attainment in the intellect of each and every thing, each according to its aspect. Certainly this person too must constantly draw upon himself the pure and holy waters — the aspect of the waters of supernal Chochmah and the holy Torah — since he must engage and recognize at every turn a new wisdom — corresponding to each new dish's aspect of holy sparks of Chochmah clothed within it. But since not every mind can bear this, and not every person merits to attain all of this in detail, this washing is only optional — not established as a mitzvah — only the first washing is established, to purify oneself from any impurity and connect oneself in general at least to the holy Torah and Chochmah clothed in every thing.

סִימָן ר״ס וְכוּ׳ — הִלְכוֹת מִילָה

[§1]
The laws of circumcision. For the orlah [foreskin] alludes to the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — which is the aspect of the general totality of non-Jews — encompassed in the klippa of Esav and Yishmael — as is known. And therefore Israel must remove it. And therefore: the general strengthening of the yetzer hara — which introduces the spirit of folly into a person — is also called orlah: *"circumcise the foreskin of your heart"* [Devarim 10:16] — and the Targum translates: "remove the foolishness of your heart." And since the essential strengthening of the spirit of folly of the yetzer hara is in this desire — the aspect of what our Sages taught on the verse: "when his wife goes astray" — and as cited in the holy Zohar: the essential root of the evil inclination is to reveal nakedness — therefore: through cutting the orlah — one weakens and diminishes the power of the yetzer hara — and diminishes the desire for cohabitation — as cited in their teachings. And this is the aspect of the revealing of the crown [atara] — which is revealed through the circumcision. Meaning: the illumination of holy Malchus is revealed — the aspect of: "a worthy woman is the crown of her husband." And in the Kiddush Levanah [sanctification of the moon] one says: "that she should renew herself as a crown of glory." And through this one merits the light of intellect and holy mochin — until one merits to attain Hashem through every thing in the world. And this too is the aspect of the revealing of the crown — for the mochin are the essential crown — the aspect of: "and their crowns upon their heads" — said regarding the righteous in the future — as explained elsewhere. And this too is the aspect of what our Sages taught [Megillah 15b]: "in the future the Holy One will be a crown upon the head of every righteous person" — etc. And this is the aspect of what our Sages taught [Bamidbar Rabbah, Naso, ch. 12]: "this is the matter that Hashem commanded — perform" — regarding circumcision. "And the honor of Hashem shall appear to you" — and likewise: regarding Avraham — when he was circumcised — it is said: "and Hashem appeared to him" — etc. — as stated. For through this one merits the revelation of His divinity — that one shall attain His divinity through all things of the world. And this is the aspect of: *"and from my flesh I shall behold G-d"* [Iyov 19:26] — and as our Sages taught. And this is the aspect of: circumcision on the eighth — corresponding to the light of Chochmah — the aspect of ches — as stated. And therefore: one circumcises only by day — for the light of Chochmah is the aspect of the shining light that goes and shines until the day is established. And therefore: a sick person — the aspect of damage to the life-force — damage to Chochmah — as understood also in the writings on the verse: "Hashem will support him on the bed of illness" — therefore one does not circumcise him until he recovers.

[§2]
And one waits for him seven days from the moment of recovery — in order to draw upon him anew the light of holy life-force and Chochmah — the aspect of ches — as stated. And then one circumcises him. When does the above apply? — when a fever afflicted him — etc. — for this indicates that the aspect of the sun of the sitra achra has overpowered him. And this is the aspect of the yetzer hara being called cham — for from one's own heat the person becomes ill. And likewise in other bodily illnesses — where the damage has spread to the general life-force. But if he was ill only in one of his limbs — etc. — one circumcises him immediately after he recovers. But if his eyes pained him severely — that is like a bodily illness. For the eyes are named for wisdom — for one must always gaze with an open eye upon the light of wisdom in every thing — as stated. And this is the aspect of: "I have made a covenant with my eyes" [Iyov 31:1] — etc. And this is the aspect of the eye-lights alluded to in the letters mem-lamed of the word milah. And this is also the aspect of the ein chasadim [eye of kindness] — as cited in the kavanos — for the root of kindness is in Chochmah — as stated many times. And this too is the aspect of: chei-es lights — eight kindnesses — cited in the kavanos — the aspect of ches mentioned.

[§3]
(And the hidden matters are not our domain.) And this is the aspect of milah and peri'ah and metzitzah. Milah [the cut] corresponds to the aspect of nullifying the yetzer hara — when it incites a person to actual transgression — G-d forbid — which is the actual orlah. Peri'ah [the uncovering] corresponds to the way of the yetzer hara — to dress itself in mitzvos — and then one needs great alacrity and cleverness — not to listen to it. And even so: one should not leave and abandon the mitzvah because of this — but rather: distinguish and separate the good from the evil — and perform the mitzvah with such wisdom and intellect — that one not come through it to transgression as the yetzer hara desires and intends — G-d forbid. And this is the aspect of peri'ah — which exposes the membrane and splits it — and leaves it to cleave and be included in the flesh of the crown — and does not tear and cut it off entirely. The meaning is as above: one does this in such a manner that everything is encompassed in holiness — and no mishap or damage or stumbling emerges from it — G-d forbid. And therefore: one who performed the milah but not the peri'ah — it is as if one did not circumcise. For the yetzer hara can yet overpower one — G-d forbid — through this aspect — of dressing itself in mitzvos — to bring one to transgression — which is the aspect of complete orlah — G-d forbid.

[§4]
And afterwards one sucks the blood [metzitzah] — and through this one completely subdues the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — the klippa of wicked Esav the red man of blood — completely — so that there be no hold on the soul of Israel even in potential. For sometimes one subdues the yetzer hara — so that it cannot actually overpower to bring to actual transgression — G-d forbid — even through the aspect of dressing itself in mitzvos — and even so there is a hold on it in the aspect of potential — G-d forbid. And then the person is not yet safe from it — for it lurks against one like a bear — to cause one to fall in its net each time — G-d forbid. And this hold — since it is only in the inner dimension alone — in the aspect of potential — as stated — is therefore not in the category of the orlah — and not in the category of the skin of the peri'ah — since it is not visible or recognizable at all. And it is only in the aspect of blood — where is the root of its hold in potential — G-d forbid. And therefore: one must suck it out well — until no blood remains except good and holy blood — in which there is no hold of evil at all — even in potential. And then the light of the crown is revealed — the aspect of drawing the light of these rectifications in their fullness. And therefore: one who is born circumcised also needs to draw a drop of covenant blood — in order to nullify from him even the aspect of the hold of evil in potential — as stated. And corresponding to these three aspects — one draws the aspects of three rectifications. For through cutting the orlah — the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — which grows strong to do complete evil in actual deed — G-d forbid — and when one cuts it — the aspect of holy Malchus is strengthened — for when this one rises that one falls — etc.

[§5]
And the rectification through Torah study is the aspect of the rectification drawn through peri'ah — through which one distinguishes good from evil — and the evil falls — and the good remains in its fullness. And this is what our Sages taught: "all that the Merciful One forbids — He permits for us an equivalent." Meaning: through this one clarifies the good even from the aspect of evil — as stated. And through subduing the evil also at its root — in the aspect of potential — which is the aspect of metzitzah — through this one merits the revelation of the light of supernal Chochmah — which is in the aspect of potential — as is known — the aspect of: Chochmah — the letters koach mah [power of mah] — as cited. And this is the aspect of what is said in the verse: "praiseworthy is one whom You choose and draw near to dwell in Your courtyards" [Tehillim 65:5] — this corresponds to holy Malchus — the aspect of chatzros Hashem. "We shall be satisfied with the goodness of Your house" — this corresponds to Torah — for "there is no good except Torah." And it is the aspect of: the House of Bereishis. "Your holy Sanctuary" — this corresponds to the light of Chochmah — called holy — as is known — and is the essential inner dimension — the aspect of: "a point within his sanctuary." And see the holy Zohar. And everything converges to one place. And therefore after the circumcision one blesses over wine — which alludes to Malchus and likewise to Chochmah — as stated many times. And therefore one prays then for the life and survival of the infant — for through these rectifications the prayer is accepted. And therefore one gives then the Israelite name to the infant — for a name alludes also to the aspects of these rectifications — and the name is the root of all the names of the children of Israel. And this is what is said: "just as he has entered the covenant — so may he enter Torah." This corresponds to Torah study — through which is the essential drawing of these rectifications. And this: "and to the wedding canopy" — this corresponds to the aspect of the source of supernal Chochmah — from which the light of the sun goes and shines — the aspect of: "and he is as a groom going out from his canopy" [Tehillim 19:6] — as understood in the holy Zohar. And: "and to good deeds" — this corresponds to holy Malchus — nestled in the world of action — as is known. And this: *"and I said to you: in your blood — live"* [Yechezkel 16:6] — for through the blood of circumcision one merits the drawing of these rectifications — which are the essential aspect of life — as stated. And this is the aspect of the chashmal cited in the kavanos and in the holy Zohar — for our Sages taught: chashmal is from the language of chash [silence] and mal [speech] — the aspect of the general totality of these rectifications. For Chochmah is the aspect of chash — the aspect of: "silence is a fence for wisdom." Mal is from the aspect of Malchus-of-mouth — the aspect of speech. And therefore: the orlah and the blood of metzitzah are placed in earth — the aspect of what our Sages taught regarding subduing the yetzer hara: let one recall the day of death — the aspect of: "for you are dust and to dust you shall return." And also: earth alludes to holy Malchus — as is known. And this is the aspect of: "all was from the dust" — and our Sages taught: even the globe of the sun — for one cannot merit the light of the intellect — the aspect of the sun — except through the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of dust — as stated. And therefore the custom is to make a chair for Eliyahu — and it is explained in Siddur Kol Yaakov that this is because he is of the aspect of Malchus — etc. — as stated — for through him Heavenly Kingship was so greatly revealed: "and all the people saw — etc. — and they said: Hashem — He is G-d" — etc. And therefore: when the time of the coming of Mashiach arrives — when His Kingdom is fully revealed — in the aspect of: "and saviors shall ascend Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esav — and the Kingdom shall be Hashem's" [Ovadyah 1:21] — therefore Eliyahu will come first to announce this — for it is from his aspect. And therefore one must say with one's mouth that it is the chair of Eliyahu — for Malchus — etc. And this is the aspect of the sanctity of the sandak — who is like ketores [incense]. Meaning: since upon his knees is the mitzvah of circumcision performed — through which is the essential subduing of the yetzer hara — therefore he is in the aspect of ketores — as explained in the holy Zohar, part 2, 218b: "since the breaking of the yetzer hara is certainly from all sides through the ketores — etc. — there is nothing in the world to break the sitra achra like ketores" — etc. — and it concludes: "and one is saved from all judgments — and from the judgment of the other kingdom." And see further on this in Zohar Chadash, Shir HaShirim, 80b. And therefore: the woman brings the infant to the synagogue — since she is of the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of: "a woman who fears Hashem." And therefore the mohalim [circumcisers] customarily pray on the day of circumcision — for through this the prayer is accepted. And therefore the sandak and the mohel go up to the Torah. For the essential drawing of these rectifications is through Torah. And the reason the sandak precedes the mohel — see the reason in the latter-day legal authorities. And therefore a feast is made on the day of circumcision — for through the drawing of these rectifications — through this is the essential rectification of the meal — as stated many times. And therefore circumcision overrides tzara'as. For through it the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — called tzara'as and baheres and nega — is pushed away. And therefore one cuts it together with the orlah — for it is one aspect with it. And therefore: circumcision overrides Shabbos — for through it one draws the light of supernal Chochmah — which is the root of the holiness of Shabbos — the aspect of: "for it is holy" — as is known. And this is what our Sages taught [Nedarim 31b]: "I vow to have no benefit from uncircumcised ones" — forbidden even from circumcised non-Jews — for they are the essential aspect of orlah. And this is what they said there: "the foreskin is repulsive — for the wicked are disgraced through it" — etc. — for from there comes all wickedness — and it is repulsive and shameful — the opposite of holy grace — as explained within. And this: "great is circumcision — for thirteen covenants were made regarding it" — corresponding to the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded — the general totality of Torah discourses. And corresponding to the thirteen attributes of mercy — the aspect of the general totality of prayer. "Great is circumcision — for it overrides Shabbos" — as stated. "Great is circumcision — that Moshe was not spared for it" — etc. — and even though he himself is the aspect of the sun — the aspect of Chochmah. "Great is circumcision — that none of the commandments that Avraham our father performed made him complete — until he circumcised himself." For sometimes the yetzer hara also dresses in mitzvos — and therefore the essential fullness of the mitzvos is when one completely subdues the yetzer hara. And also: through this one merits the light of Chochmah — the essential fullness — the aspect of: "if you acquired daas — what do you lack?" And this is the explanation of: "walk before Me and be wholesome" [Bereishis 17:1] — meaning: may you merit the light of holy intellect — the aspect of Yaakov the wholesome man — as explained within. Alternative explanation: "great is circumcision — for were it not for it — the Holy One would not have created His world." For the essential creation of the world was b'gin d'yishtamodain leih — and to this one cannot merit except through the mitzvah of circumcision — as stated. And see there further [32b, 267]: The laws of slaves. It is a positive commandment for the master to circumcise his slaves — etc. For even though they were born from non-Jews — who are from the aspect of the yetzer hara — the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — the aspect of orlah — even so: since they were sold to an Israelite and entered under his authority — who is of the aspect of the yetzer tov — holy Malchus — therefore one must circumcise them — and cut their orlah — in order to remove from them the filth of the yetzer hara — the kingdom of the sitra achra. And there are distinctions in law between a yeled bais [home-born slave] — circumcised on the eighth — for one can draw upon him the glimmer from the aspect of the light of ches mentioned. And a miknath kesef [purchased slave] — circumcised on the day he was acquired — for one only needs to cut his orlah in order to encompass him somewhat in holy Malchus. And there are details in this in the Shulchan Aruch — and all is explained according to the above. And therefore one informs him of the essentials of the religion — etc. — and in the presence of three one converts him somewhat — in order to draw upon him the aspect of the waters of holy daas — through which one merits to know Him — even so he does not yet have the full status of Israel — and is obligated only in commandments in which women are obligated. And therefore: when he is freed and wishes to enter the holiness of Israel fully — he then requires immersion again before three — and this will be explained below. And therefore the slave is acquired by his master through money and deed and taking possession — corresponding to three aspects: money corresponds to the aspect of Chochmah — the brain — the aspect of: "in the shadow of wisdom — in the shadow of money" [Koheles 7:12] — the aspect of: "from the right side — the white brain — as silver." The deed corresponds to the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of action — as stated. And therefore the slave acquires himself to go out to full freedom — also through three things: through money — corresponding to Chochmah. Through deed — corresponding to Torah. And through primary limbs [roshei evarim] — corresponding to Malchus. For the slave himself is from the aspect of Malchus (see Maurai Or) — and his essential fullness is from what his master illuminates to him from the light of his holiness and wisdom — through which he somewhat encompasses him in Israel's holiness. Even so he is subjugated to him for his work. And therefore: if his master struck him — he goes free through tooth and eye — which allude to the aspect of Chochmah.

[§6]
For there are thirty-two teeth — corresponding to thirty-two paths of Chochmah — as is known. And likewise: eyes are named for wisdom — as stated. And likewise in other primary limbs — which also allude to the aspects of life-force and wisdom in that limb. For the head is from the aspect of reishis Chochmah. It emerges: not only did the master not illuminate to him the aspect of life-force and wisdom — but even damaged the diminishment of the aspect of life-force and wisdom in him. Therefore the Torah penalized him — that his slave goes out to full freedom. And one compels the master to write him a bill of manumission — and then he is no longer subjugated to his master — to receive holiness from him. Only he receives life-force from the general holiness of Israel — in which the aspect of life-force and holiness from the light of holy Chochmah shines — as stated. And therefore: he does not go out to freedom until the master does this with intention — flowing from the aspect of his own wisdom. And therefore: it is not permitted to free one's slave — unless for the sake of a mitzvah. For who knows whether he is at the level to merit Israel's holiness fully — since at his root he is from non-Jews — only he was sold to an Israelite. And therefore: his merit is to be subjugated to Israel forever — in the aspect of: "forever shall you work them" [Vayikra 25:46]. And if one frees him — it is possible that this is a damage and stumbling block — and also for the master and owner. For one may thereby give some illumination and flow to those who are proximate to the side of the sitra achra — G-d forbid. And therefore: it is permitted to free him for the sake of a mitzvah. For since the foundation of the matter of manumission is immediately encompassed in a matter of mitzvah — the aspect of holy Malchus — therefore there is no longer concern for all of this — for "a guardian of the commandment shall know no evil" — and presumably there will be no damage or stumbling through this.

[§8] General and specific blessings — and this itself is the matter of why our Sages instituted both general and specific blessings — and within the specific ones there are themselves levels of general and specific — such as borei pri ha'adamah [who creates the fruit of the ground] being general, and borei pri ha'etz [who creates the fruit of the tree] more specific — and wine, due to its importance, has a further specific blessing: borei pri hagafen. And likewise for bread types — borei minei mezonos [who creates species of grain foods] is general, and bread, due to its importance, has the specific blessing HaMotzi — and all of this is understood and explained according to this approach. For our Sages taught: "Blessed is Hashem day by day" [Tehillim 68:20] — "each day give [thanks for that day's blessings]" — for each act of Hashem is for His sake — and all the variations between one day and the next — certainly each contains a wondrous wisdom of how to draw close to Hashem through it, in a new closeness and new knowledge. And therefore each day one must bless according to [that day's blessings].

סִימָן רס״ו — מִי שֶׁבָּא בַדֶּרֶךְ

 

 
 [§1]
 And this is what [the Sages] said: 
 one wh

o is traveling and Shabbos overtakes him on the road — 
 he may not place his purse upon his donkey — 
 for he is commanded regarding [the donkey's] resting — 
 but should give his purse to a non-Jew — etc.

For even a donkey — which is an impure animal and is from the aspect of the sitra achra — 
 nonetheless, since it belongs to a Jew, 
 it has already gained some hold in the side of holiness — 
 for it has become a chariot toward it — 
 and therefore one is commanded regarding its resting.

And therefore he gives his purse to the non-Jew 
 who has no part in holiness. 
 And moreover — this was only permitted regarding 
 money that already belongs to him — 
 for the money of a Jew too has a root in holiness — 
 as is stated elsewhere: 
 *"in the shadow of wisdom, in the shadow of silver"* [Koheles 7:12] — 
 and likewise holy wealth is from the aspect of holy Malchus — as stated above.

But money that has not yet come into the Jew's hands — 
 such as if he found a lost object — 
 he may not give it even to the non-Jew — 
 for it is forbidden to damage the holiness of Shabbos even through a non-Jew — as stated.

And therefore if there is no non-Jew with him — 
 he is permitted to place [the purse] upon the donkey — 
 but only in the manner described in the Shulchan Aruch — see there — 
 and from this the other matters explained in this Siman are understood.

[§9] And wine, due to its great importance — for it gladdens G-d and men, and one recites song only over wine — and our Sages taught: "wine and fragrance make the mind sharp" [Yoma 76b] — and from this the holy life-force clothed within it is most visible and apparent — therefore one must bless it with a specific blessing. And likewise, change of location constitutes an interruption during a meal — for Hashem, as it were, contracts Himself and alludes hints of wisdom to each person through each particular thing according to place and time — as explained in the discourse Meketz Zikaron, Siman 54 — and therefore change of location is also considered a change in this matter. And likewise the matter of things that require an after-blessing specifically in their place [b'mekomam] — due to their importance — and all of this is understood according to the above.

[§1] For all the time that Hashem, as it were, desires the continued existence of the sitra achra — for the sake of [preserving] the power of free choice — one must therefore draw for it also some spark of holy life-force — but only enough for its sustenance and in great contraction — and through this specifically one subdues it — as is understood in the discourse Marikim Sakeihem, Siman 17 — and this is elaborated much in the holy Zohar. And this is the matter of the mayim acharonim [final waters] taken after the meal — for since eating is a physical, animalistic matter — it being one of the things in which man resembles an animal — as our Sages taught — and in particular since the implements of eating are from the side of Esav — as stated — it is impossible for some degree of foolishness not to gain hold through this. Therefore one gives them their portion through the final waters — so that they not grow stronger, G-d forbid.

[§2] And our Sages taught that one takes final waters on account of Melach Sedomis [Sodomite salt], which blinds the eyes — and a trace [of it] is mixed among the pure salt, for in the holy salt [of the Ketores] there is hidden also a trace of this. And in the intentions of the Ketores it is explained that Melach Sedomis is the secret of Tidal king of nations [Bereishis 14:1] — and the Midrash explains that Tidal king of nations alludes to the kingdom of Edom — etc. — and it is known that the exile of Edom encompasses both Esav and Yishmael, who are the clouds that blind the eyes — and therefore Melach Sedomis blinds the eyes — which are the aspect of Chochmah — as it is written: *"and the eyes of them both were opened"* [Bereishis 3:7] — and Rashi explains: this was said regarding wisdom.

[§3] And it has already been explained above that Chochmah is in the aspect of salt — and therefore there is found among a kor of salt one kernel of Sodomite salt — so that they too should have some nourishment from it in great contraction. And in order that they not grow stronger and blind the eyes — meaning confuse a person from looking with open eyes at the holy wisdom and intellect in every thing — one must take the final waters — as stated. And this is what is explained in the kavanos and cited in the Siddur Kol Yaakov: that the final waters serve to drive away the sitra achra from the table and give them their portion — etc. — and this is what our Sages taught: on account of Melach Sedomis which blinds the eyes — which is the secret of the strong klippa — etc. — which is the secret of the shakyan — the old and foolish king — etc. — see there — and it corresponds to our matter — for the kingdom of the sitra achra — the aspect of the yetzer hara — is the Satan — the aspect of Esav — the aspect of the old and foolish king — for "the fool desires not understanding" [Mishlei 18:2] — as explained within. And therefore: melech zakein u'ksil [old and foolish king] together with the word count in numerical value equals Esav.
